securityInformation.title: Nodes can delete themselves by adding an OwnerReference
securityInformation.description: A vulnerability exists in the NodeRestriction admission controller where node users can delete their corresponding node object by patching themselves with an OwnerReference to a cluster-scoped resource. If the OwnerReference resource does not exist or is subsequently deleted, the given node object will be deleted via garbage collection. By default, node users are authorized for create and patch requests but not delete requests against their node object. Since the NodeRestriction admission controller does not prevent patching OwnerReferences, a compromised node could leverage this vulnerability to delete and then recreate its node object with modified taints or labels.

securityInformation.title: Nodes can bypass dynamic resource allocation authorization checks
securityInformation.description: A vulnerability exists in the NodeRestriction admission controller where nodes can bypass dynamic resource allocation authorization checks. When the DynamicResourceAllocation feature gate is enabled, the controller properly validates resource claim statuses during pod status updates but fails to perform equivalent validation during pod creation. This allows a compromised node to create mirror pods that access unauthorized dynamic resources, potentially leading to privilege escalation.

securityInformation.title: Node Denial of Service via Kubelet Checkpoint API
securityInformation.description: A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where a large number of container checkpoint requests made to the unauthenticated kubelet read-only HTTP endpoint may cause a Node Denial of Service by filling the Node's disk.

issueContext.title: UserInfo.UID is not passed by client-go
issueContext.body:
It looks UserInfo.UID is newer than other fields and while #49677 added it SubjectAccessReviewSpec for webhook authorization, it's still not being sent by client-go in headers. Also there is no flag in APIServer to process those headers. As a result all authorizers needing that, may not work correctly for SubjectAccessReviews made by kube-aggregator extensions.

**What happened**:

Our webhook authorizer, authorizes users using UserInfo.UID. It's missing in SubjectAccessReviews created by kube-aggregator extensions (our case was state metrics), resulting authorizer to not work.

**What you expected to happen**:

I except All fields that is filled by authenticator be present for authorizer and I think it's valid to have an authorizer to use UID.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Make authentication webhook that fills SubjectAccessReviewSpec.UID. You will see there UID is missing from SubjectAccessReviewSpecs made by a kube-aggregator extension.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

UserInfo.UID is not passed to client-go round-tripper [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/transport/round_trippers.go#L118) and [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/transport/round_trippers.go#L101) and impersonate config do nothing for it. There is also no api-server flag to get it from headers.

enrichment.problem: UserInfo.UID header was never read by kube-apiserver, so UID from authenticators was omitted from SubjectAccessReview requests generated by kube-aggregator extensions, breaking authorizers (e.g., webhook authorizer) that rely on UID.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using requestheader authentication with aggregated API servers (kube-aggregator extensions) and any authorizer that expects UserInfo.UID, such as webhook authorizers.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new flag `--requestheader-uid-headers` for kube-apiserver to specify which request headers contain the authenticating user's UID (suggested value `X-Remote-Uid`). When set, the `kube-system/extension-apiserver-authentication` ConfigMap is populated with the header name, enabling the apiserver to propagate UID to authorizers.
enrichment.impact: Authorizers that depend on UID now receive the correct value for SARs from aggregated APIs, restoring correct authorization decisions for extensions such as state metrics and improving overall security and consistency of requestheader authentication.

enrichment.problem: When a container's StartupProbe succeeded enough times (reached successThreshold), the probe was not stopped and continued to run, causing extra probe executions especially when periodSeconds was shorter than the probe processing time.
enrichment.affected: Any pod that defines a StartupProbe, particularly those with long start‑up processes where the probe interval is shorter than the probe's execution time.

enrichment.impact: Pods using StartupProbe no longer experience unnecessary probe runs, reducing load and avoiding side‑effects from duplicate executions, leading to more predictable startup behavior.

issueContext.title: minimumGracePeriodInSeconds from eviction config can increase the grace period
issueContext.body:
/kind bug
/sig node
cc @mtaufen 

We use the gracePeriodOverride from the eviction manager (which is set to m.config.MaxPodGracePeriodSeconds for soft evictions) as the gracePeriodOverride that we pass to `killPod()`
This is consumed here:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_container.go#L568
Where it overrides whatever the pod's DeletionGracePeriodSeconds and Spec.TerminationGracePeriodSeconds.  Either the name is misleading, or it isn't actually a maximum, but rather is just "the" grace period for soft evictions.

enrichment.problem: During a soft eviction, the kubelet overwrote the pod's spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds with MaxPodGracePeriodSeconds, effectively ignoring any custom termination grace period set by the user.

enrichment.fix: Introduced the AllowOverwriteTerminationGracePeriodSeconds feature gate. When enabled, the pod's original terminationGracePeriodSeconds is preserved during soft evictions, restoring the previous behavior.
enrichment.impact: Users can once again rely on custom termination grace periods for graceful shutdowns during node pressure events, avoiding unexpectedly long termination delays and giving better control over pod lifecycle.

issueContext.title: Graceful node shutdown doesn't wait for volume teardown
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

We have observed that after a node is preempted, pods using persistent volumes take 6+ minutes to restart. This happens when a volume was not able to be cleanly unmounted (indicated by updating `Node.Status.VolumesInUse`), which causes the Attach/Detach controller (in kube-controller-manager) to wait for 6 minutes before issuing a force detach. In addition to a long pod restart period, an unclean mount could also cause data corruption.

From the logs we've observed the following non-ideal behaviors, which I think reduces to the same issue that we only check for containers' being terminated and not their volumes.

1. The CSI driver running on the node gets terminated before the workload's volumes get unmounted. This causes unmount to fail. In our case, the CSI driver is part of the `system-node-critical" class, but since we don't wait for volumes to be unmounted, we move on to shutting down the critical pods.

3. The OS gets shutdown before volume teardown is completed, even if there is still time left in the `shutdownGracePeriod`. In our case, the `shutdownGracePeriod` is set to 30 seconds, however we see that the node got shutdown in 10 seconds, even while unmount has not succeeded.

kubelet.log
```
Jan 17 21:48:18 ip-10-0-1-208 kubelet[950]: I0117 21:48:18.460409     950 setters.go:548] "Node became not ready" node="ip-10-0-1-208" condition={Type:Ready Status:False LastHeartbeatTime:2023-01-17 21:48:18.46035065 +0000 UTC m=+1235.025577092 LastTransitionTime:2023-01-17 21:48:18.46035065 +0000 UTC m=+1235.025577092 Reason:KubeletNotReady Message:node is shutting down}
...
Jan 17 21:48:27 ip-10-0-1-208 kubelet[950]: E0117 21:48:27.126414     950 nestedpendingoperations.go:348] Operation for "{volumeName:kubernetes.io/csi/ebs.csi.aws.com^vol-00477959568e1db98 podName: nodeName:}" failed. No retries permitted until 2023-01-17 21:48:35.126400526 +0000 UTC m=+1251.691626967 (durationBeforeRetry 8s). Error: UnmountDevice failed for volume

enrichment.problem: During node shutdown the controller did not wait for CSI drivers to finish detaching and unmounting persistent volumes, so volumes could remain attached or unmounted, leading to long pod restart times and potential data corruption.
enrichment.affected: Nodes being shut down (e.g., preempted or drained) with pods that use CSI‑managed persistent volumes; workloads on those pods could experience delayed restarts or corrupted data.
enrichment.fix: The node shutdown controller now makes a best‑effort pause for CSI drivers to complete volume teardown, honoring the pod priority groups before proceeding with shutdown.
enrichment.impact: Graceful node shutdown now respects volume cleanup, reducing pod downtime, preventing possible data loss, and ensuring the shutdownGracePeriod is effectively used.

bugOrRegression.description: Improved the scalability of the PVC Protection Controller by batch-processing PVCs by namespace with lazy live pod listing.
bugOrRegression.author: hungnguyen243
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: Improve PVC Protection Controller's scalability by batch-processing PVCs by namespace with lazy live pod listing.

issueContext.title: PVCProtectionController can be slow for larger clusters
issueContext.body:
## References
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/76703
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/75980
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/80492
* https://github.com/kubernetes/design-proposals-archive/blob/main/storage/postpone-pvc-deletion-if-used-in-a-pod.md

## Overview

As described [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/design-proposals-archive/blob/main/storage/postpone-pvc-deletion-if-used-in-a-pod.md) PVC protection controller uses logic that postpones deletion of PVC in case it is used by Pod. When the Pod is deleted and PVC is marked for deletion as well (by setting `deletionTimestamp`) the PVC protection controllers ensures that all references to the PVC has been deleted and no Pod is using it.

PVC protection controller processes PVC one by one checking if there is still a Pod that has any reference to it. If not, the finalizer is removed and PVC is deleted from the cluster.

## The problem

Some time ago the [issue](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/76703) was filled that described race condition in PVC protection controller. Basically the logic used and relied only on Pod's informer cache which could be potentially outdated and PVC protection controller could deleted PVC that it's still being used (has been recently attached). There was also [MR](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/80492) that fixed it.

The problem with the new logic is that it has really slow/inefficient performance which is in order of `O(m * n)` (where `m` is the number of PVCs to be processed and `n` is the number of Pods in the cluster). [Someone even pointed it out](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/80492#discussion_r306743513) in the MR but it wasn't sufficiently measured/analyzed. For active larger cluster 1k+ where there is a lot of Pods/PVCs being created and deleted the PVC protection controller is too slow to process everything. This causes large number of PVCs still being in the cluster

enrichment.problem: The PVC Protection Controller processed PVCs individually and relied on a full pod list per PVC, causing high CPU and latency in large clusters when cleaning up PVCs, leading to slow PVC deletion operations.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with large numbers of PersistentVolumeClaims and pods that delete PVCs; administrators and workloads that rely on timely PVC cleanup.
enrichment.fix: The controller now batches PVCs by namespace and performs lazy live pod listing, reducing the number of pod list calls and enabling more efficient, scalable processing of PVC finalizers.
enrichment.impact: PVC deletion and finalizer removal become faster and less resource‑intensive, especially in clusters with many PVCs and pods, improving overall control‑plane performance and reducing deletion‑related delays.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a bug where pods bound to a PersistentVolume with `nodeAffinity` using the hostname label could be scheduled to the wrong node or fail scheduling when the hostname label of a node did not match the node name.

bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: Fix a bug when the hostname label of a node does not match the node name, pods bound to a PV with nodeAffinity using the hostname may be scheduled to the wrong node or experience scheduling failures.

enrichment.problem: When a node's `kubernetes.io/hostname` label did not match the node's name, pods bound to a PersistentVolume that used nodeAffinity based on the hostname could be scheduled to the wrong node or fail to schedule.
enrichment.affected: Pods using PersistentVolumes with nodeAffinity based on the hostname label, and nodes where the hostname label differs from the node name.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler’s nodeAffinity evaluation for PV binding now correctly uses the node's hostname label regardless of whether it matches the node name, ensuring pods are placed on the intended node or remain unscheduled if no matching node exists.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on PersistentVolume nodeAffinity for placement will now be scheduled accurately, preventing accidental placement on unintended nodes and eliminating scheduling failures in clusters with custom hostnames.

issueContext.title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] Backoff problem when quickly reverting resize patch

### What happened?

While working on #125202 , issue with backoff was discovered resulting to slow reconcile when quickly reverting resize patch. This can be reproduced please check https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/125205#issuecomment-2203184854 ,  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/125205#issuecomment-2143527472.

issueContext.title: Creating a CRD with broken converter webhook prevents GC controller from initialization
issueContext.body:
#### What happened:

Creating a CRD with broken converter webhook prevents GC controller from initialization, which breaks on informer sync. Additionally, this issue is not visible until gc controller restarts - dynamically added crd resources with non-working converter webhook do not break running GC.

#### What you expected to happen:

GC controller should initialize with available informers. CRDs with broken converter webhook should not prevent GC controller from working on other resources.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

1. Create a cluster
1. Create a CRD (1_crd.yaml)
1. Create a CR (2_crd.yaml)
1. Change CRD to add another version and webhook converter (3_crd.yaml)
1. Restart kube-controll-manager
1. Add deployment
1. Delete deployment
1. Check that pod from deployment is not GC'ed

[gc-bug.zip](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/files/6305426/gc-bug.zip)

enrichment.problem: The garbage collector controller could become permanently blocked when its cache failed to sync (e.g., due to a broken converter webhook on a CRD). When the informer for a particular resource type cannot be listed or watched, the GC stopped processing all other resources, leaving objects with `blockOwnerDeletion:true` unknown to the collector.
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes cluster where the garbage collector controller is unable to sync a resource type (e.g., CRDs with broken conversion webhooks). Objects that rely on `blockOwnerDeletion:true` in the unsynced type may not be GC'ed, but the rest of the cluster continues to function correctly.
enrichment.fix: The GC controller now detects a cache sync failure and skips the problematic resource type, allowing it to continue garbage‑collecting other resources. The `blockOwnerDeletion` behavior remains best‑effort for unsynced resources.
enrichment.impact: Clusters no longer experience a complete halt of garbage collection due to a single faulty resource type. This reduces the chance of orphaned objects accumulating and improves overall controller‑manager stability, especially for clusters using custom resources with conversion webhooks.

issueContext.title: Kubelet - failed to initialize top level QOS containers: root container [kubepods] doesn't exist
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

Starting the kubelet the first time after a system reboot,  the kubelet fails with:
`E0125 00:20:56.003890    2172 kubelet.go:1466] "Failed to start ContainerManager" err="failed to initialize top level QOS containers: root container [kubepods] doesn't exist"`

Which, sort of is a lie.   The root cause is actually that `cpuset` does not exist in `/sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.subtree_control` 

After the kubelet exits, systemd restarts in,  and then all is fine after that,  until the next time the OS is restarted.  

I tried to track it down,  create.go does add the cpuset to `cgroup.subtree_control`,  and it remains there until `common.go:setUnitProperties()` is executed,  at which time `cpuset` appears to be disabled and disappears.  The other controllers are unaffected.   On the subsequent kubelet restart, `cpuset` does get added again,  and remains after the call to setUnitProperties().   

### What did you expect to happen?

I would expect the kubelet to start and not exit on all starts of the kubelet. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

The OS I am using is RHEL 9 on s390x.   
1) Boot the OS
2) Start the kubelet (I start with `kubeadm init` or `kubeadm join`.
3) Observer the kubelet starts,  fails, and then restarts.   Subsequent restarts of the kubelet are successful until the OS rebooted. (Likely due to after a reboot, the /sys/fs/cgroups is fresh,  unlike subsequent restarts of the kubelet)


### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

enrichment.problem: On nodes using cgroup v2 with the systemd cgroup manager, the kubelet sometimes fails to start after a system reboot, emitting `failed to initialize top level QOS containers: root container [kubepods] doesn't exist`. The root cause is that the cpuset controller is removed from `/sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.subtree_control`, causing the top‑level QOS containers to be missing.
enrichment.affected: Nodes running the kubelet with cgroup v2 and the systemd cgroup manager (e.g., RHEL 9, s390x) could not start the kubelet after a reboot, causing the node to be unschedulable until the kubelet restarted.

issueContext.title: HTTP2_PING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS+HTTP2_READ_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS > 40s will cause all node NotReady
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

The controller-manager node-lifecycle-controller watches node lease and update `nodeHealthMap` probeTimestamp , and it check node probeTimestamp is before `now - node-monitor-grace-period`. The node-monitor-grace-period default value is 40s.

When the client connection lost, the lease watcher cannot receive new event. With the http2 health check,   HTTP2_PING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS default is 30s, HTTP2_READ_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS default is  15s, it will delay 45s to kill http2  connection.  

During this period, node-lifecycle-controller will mark all nodes NotReady.

Here are some logs

```
I1103 23:00:28.464015       1 node_lifecycle_controller.go:1097] node 10.0.10.240 hasn't been updated for 40.010894415s. Last Ready is: &NodeCondition{Type:Ready,Status:True,LastHeartbeatTime:2023-11-03 22:57:18 +0800 CST,LastTransitionTime:2023-04-21 14:39:17 +0800 CST,Reason:KubeletReady,Message:kubelet is posting ready status,}

W1103 23:00:41.408493       1 reflector.go:441] k8s.io/client-go/informers/factory.go:134: watch of *v1.Lease ended with: an error on the server ("unable to decode an event from the watch stream: http2: client connection lost") has prevented the request from succeeding
```

### What did you expect to happen?

When the http2 connection lost, the watch should stop as soon as possible. The reflector should relist resource, and node-lifecycle-controller should not mark all node NotReady.

HTTP2_PING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS+HTTP2_READ_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS should be less than 40s.


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Find the controller-manager node-lifecycle-controller watch client srcIP:srcPort. Drop all tcp package send into srcIP:srcPort.
2. Wait for more than 40 seconds, all node will be marked NotReady
3. All node will be Ready after some seconds.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version
# Server

enrichment.problem: When the HTTP/2 connection between the controller-manager and the API server is lost, the node lease watch does not receive updates for up to 45 seconds (HTTP2_PING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 30s + HTTP2_READ_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 15s). The node-lifecycle-controller then compares the last node heartbeat to the default node-monitor-grace-period (40s) and incorrectly marks all nodes NotReady, causing spurious cluster-wide node failures.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that rely on the default `node-monitor-grace-period` (the majority of installations). The node-lifecycle-controller could incorrectly mark every node NotReady after a temporary loss of the HTTP/2 watch connection.
enrichment.fix: Increase the default value of the `node-monitor-grace-period` flag from 40 seconds to 50 seconds, providing a buffer longer than the maximum HTTP/2 idle timeout and preventing premature NotReady transitions.
enrichment.impact: Reduces false NotReady conditions and unnecessary pod evictions, improving cluster stability and availability, especially in environments where transient HTTP/2 connection losses occur.

issueContext.title: Terminated but not GC'd Pods should not be re-admitted on kubelet restart
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

Pods that already succeeded and waiting for finalizer are being readmitted, fail to be admitted and moving from Succeeded Phase to Failed (admission failed) phase.

### What did you expect to happen?

The correct behavior would be to not try to re-admit the succeeded (or failed) Pod.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Specific case:

- Node is exposing Devices using device plugin. Device plugin is implemented as a Pod
- Job's pod that is using the Device run to completion and waiting for Job Status finalizer
- kubelet is being restarted
- DevicePlugin pod is reconnecting to the kubelet. While it is reconnecting, kubelet don't have availability of devices
- kubelet re-admits the Pod, even though it is terminated already
- kubelet marks the pod as "failed to be admitted"

But the same can happen with the variations of GC speed and other admission handlers.

### Anything else we need to know?

/sig node
/priority important-soon
/cc @bobbypage @smarterclayton 

There is also a wider issue: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/123980, that concentrates on running pods. This issue is about terminated Pods, which is less controversial.

### What would you like to be added?

Allow users to enable the PodAndContainerStatsFromCRI feature gate when using crio as the container runtime, and retrieves container stats from cri.

### Why is this needed?

Currently, crio retrieves container stats through `LegacyCadvisorStats`.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/eb729d1db72fc27f495ddf397289678b180926f1/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L712-L721
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/eb729d1db72fc27f495ddf397289678b180926f1/pkg/kubelet/cadvisor/util.go#L70-L77
That meaning it retrieves container stats from `cadvisor`. However, crio now supports retrieving container stats from cri (https://github.com/cri-o/cri-o/pull/5427).

Therefore, we should allow users to enable the `PodAndContainerStatsFromCRI` feature gate when using crio as the container runtime, and retrieves container stats from cri.

enrichment.problem: When using CRI‑O as the container runtime, kubelet collected container statistics via the legacy cAdvisor path. CRI‑O now supports providing stats through the CRI, but kubelet did not use this source even when the PodAndContainerStatsFromCRI feature gate was enabled.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use CRI‑O (or other CRI implementations that expose stats) as the container runtime and have the PodAndContainerStatsFromCRI feature gate enabled. Components that consume pod/container metrics (e.g., Horizontal Pod Autoscaler, Metrics Server) benefit from the change.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now selects the CRI stats provider when the PodAndContainerStatsFromCRI feature gate is enabled, allowing it to retrieve pod and container metrics directly from the container runtime (e.g., CRI‑O) instead of falling back to cAdvisor.
enrichment.impact: Users running CRI‑O gain more accurate and efficient resource metrics, reducing reliance on cAdvisor, improving performance of metrics‑driven features (HPA, metrics‑server) and aligning kubelet with the capabilities of modern container runtimes.

issueContext.title: kube-proxy: initialization check race leads to stale UDP conntrack
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

AKS had a customer report repeated issues in their clusters where:
1. kube-proxy would redeploy (e.g. due to AKS deploying a new kube-proxy image with CVE fixes)
2. Envoy c-ares DNS client would send repeated DNS queries to the kube-dns service VIP from the same src IP address, creating a UDP conntrack entry to the svc VIP and keeping it alive. For example, with kube-dns svc VIP 192.168.0.10, conntrack showed:
```
# conntrack -L | grep 192.168.0.10 | grep UNREPLIED
udp      17 29 src=10.120.1.150 dst=192.168.0.10 sport=49660 dport=53 [UNREPLIED] src=192.168.0.10 dst=10.120.1.150 sport=53 dport=49660 mark=0 use=1
conntrack v1.4.5 (conntrack-tools): 2273 flow entries have been shown
```

3. DNS queries to the svc VIP were blackholed until the customer manually ran a command like: `conntrack -D -p udp --src 10.120.1.150 --sport 49660`

Issue occurred only in clusters with many services and endpoints (~10k services and ~6k endpoints). However, the customer has seen this issue repeatedly for months, about 1-5 times per week across their clusters.

### What did you expect to happen?

kube-proxy code to delete stale UDP conntrack entries should have deleted the conntrack entry to kube-dns svc VIP automatically in the first sync after service and endpointslice cache is initialized.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Unfortunately, the customer said they were unable to reproduce this issue in other environments outside of their production clusters. AKS engineers were also unable to repro this issue.

**Update (2024-08-03)**: I'm now able to reproduce the issue using a DNS client that reuses the same src IP / port and clears DNAT conntrack entries between queries, in a k8s 1.29.7 cluster with 2,000 services. The bug is triggered reliably in this setup with `kubectl rollout restart -n kube-system ds/kube-proxy` The test client code, scripts, and steps to reproduce are in this repository: https://gi

enrichment.problem: A race condition during kube-proxy initialization could leave stale UDP conntrack entries for a service VIP, causing UDP traffic (e.g., DNS queries) to be dropped (blackholed).

init container &Container{Name:setup,...} start failed in pod ... : RunContainerError: error reading from server: EOF

issueContext.title: [KEP-4191] Support case when writeable layer and readable layers are on same mount but in different locations
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

In KEP-4191, we wanted to support a case where writable layers and readonly layers are on a separate disk.

This works fine but we found a bug if these layers are on the same disk but in different locations.

You can reproduce this by setting `graphRoot` and `imagestore` in crio storage to different locations.

### Why is this needed?

Kubelet should react to container storage configurations.

This false detection could cause the kubelet to treat the image as improperly layered, leading to pod start failures or unnecessary error handling.

issueContext.title: Pod status phase misses Pending transition after node reboot
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

When a kubernetes node is rebooted, all the containers running on the node are terminated and then created & started over again. When the pod has a list of init containers runing, and if the init container takes a little bit time (longer than PLEG period), the pod is supposed to have `status.phase: Pending`, but instead, during the whole operation, `status.phase` is always `Running`.

This new behavior (always has `status.phase: Running`) started when "restartable init container" was [introduced][1]. After node reboots, all the regular init containers are started one by one, so `pendingInitialization` is supposed by larger than 0 (unless the init container is completed pretty fast that PLEG doesn't catch any running init container), and should report `Pending` phase. But the behavior has changed to check further whether there are any other regular containers that have started. In the case of node reboot, all the other regular containers are already terminated, and then considered as "yes, they have started", and then no longer reported as `Pending`.

I think this behavior change is unexpected, as that violates the [definition][2] of "Running":

> // PodRunning means the pod has been bound to a node and all of the containers have been started.
	// At least one container is still running or is in the process of being restarted.

None of the containers are started or running, and they are not in the process of being started or restarted since init containers are still running.

[1]: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/099a88370d017dacf16e67306ebcdec8394fae83/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L1675-L1685
[2]: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/099a88370d017dacf16e67306ebcdec8394fae83/pkg/apis/core/types.go#L2871


### What did you expect to happen?

I expect that pods with init containers should transition into "Pending" when kubelet observed that its regular init container is still running and none of its main conta

enrichment.problem: After a node reboot, pods that have regular init containers longer than the PLEG period remain in status.phase "Running" instead of transitioning to "Pending". The kubelet incorrectly considers other regular containers as started, preventing the Pending phase despite init containers not having completed.
enrichment.affected: Pods with regular init containers on nodes that experience a reboot. Users and controllers that depend on correct pod phase information are affected.
enrichment.fix: Adjusted kubelet logic to correctly detect pending initialization after a node restart. The patch ensures that when any regular init container is still running or not yet started, the pod status.phase is set to Pending, regardless of the state of other containers.
enrichment.impact: Accurate pod phase reporting restores expected behavior for monitoring, controllers, and user tools that rely on the Pending state. Prevents false "Running" statuses that could mislead health checks and automation, improving reliability of workloads that use init containers.

My patch:

bugOrRegression.description: Improved the scalability of the PVC Protection Controller by batch-processing PVCs by namespace and implementing lazy live pod listing.
bugOrRegression.author: hungnguyen243
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: Improve PVC Protection Controller's scalability by batch-processing PVCs by namespace with lazy live pod listing.

issueContext.title: PVCProtectionController can be slow for larger clusters
issueContext.body:
## References
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/76703
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/75980
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/80492
* https://github.com/kubernetes/design-proposals-archive/blob/main/storage/postpone-pvc-deletion-if-used-in-a-pod.md

## Overview

As described [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/design-proposals-archive/blob/main/storage/postpone-pvc-deletion-if-used-in-a-pod.md) PVC protection controller uses logic that postpones deletion of PVC in case it is used by Pod. When the Pod is deleted and PVC is marked for deletion as well (by setting `deletionTimestamp`) the PVC protection controllers ensures that all references to the PVC has been deleted and no Pod is using it.

PVC protection controller processes PVC one by one checking if there is still a Pod that has any reference to it. If not, the finalizer is removed and PVC is deleted from the cluster.

## The problem

Some time ago the [issue](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/76703) was filled that described race condition in PVC protection controller. Basically the logic used and relied only on Pod's informer cache which could be potentially outdated and PVC protection controller could deleted PVC that it's still being used (has been recently attached). There was also [MR](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/80492) that fixed it.

The problem with the new logic is that it has really slow/inefficient performance which is in order of `O(m * n)` (where `m` is the number of PVCs to be processed and `n` is the number of Pods in the cluster). [Someone even pointed it out](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/80492#discussion_r306743513) in the MR but it wasn't sufficiently measured/analyzed. For active larger cluster 1k+ where there is a lot of Pods/PVCs being created and deleted the PVC protection controller is too slow to process everything. This causes large number of PVCs still being in the cluster

enrichment.problem: The PVC Protection Controller processed PVCs one‑by‑one and eagerly listed all Pods, causing high CPU usage and long delays when deleting PVCs in large clusters.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with many PersistentVolumeClaims that rely on PVC protection for safe deletion; workloads that delete PVCs could experience faster termination.
enrichment.fix: The controller now batches PVCs by namespace and performs a lazy live‑pod listing, only querying Pods when a PVC actually needs verification. This reduces API calls and CPU load, speeding up PVC deletion.
enrichment.impact: PVCs are finalized much faster, especially in clusters with many PVCs and Pods, improving overall cluster responsiveness and reducing controller‑manager load.

bugOrRegression.description: The resource/v1alpha3.ResourceSliceList filed which should have been named "metadata" but was instead named "listMeta" is now properly "metadata".
bugOrRegression.author: thockin

issueContext.title: ResourceSliceList object has `listMeta` field instead of `metadata` field
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

Listing `v1alpha3.ResourceSlice`s on v1.31.0 returns an object with a `listMeta` field instead of the standard `metadata` field for (list) objects:

```sh
$ curl -kL --cert client.pem --key client.key.pem 'https://127.0.0.1:39987/apis/resource.k8s.io/v1alpha3/resourceslices'

{
  "kind": "ResourceSliceList",
  "apiVersion": "resource.k8s.io/v1alpha3",
  "listMeta": {
    "resourceVersion": "522"
  },
  "items": []
}
```

Listing `v1alpha2.ResourceSlice`s on v1.30.3 behaves correctly:

```sh
$ curl -kL --cert client.pem --key client.key.pem 'https://127.0.0.1:34519/apis/resource.k8s.io/v1alpha2/resourceslices'

{
  "kind": "ResourceSliceList",
  "apiVersion": "resource.k8s.io/v1alpha2",
  "metadata": {
    "resourceVersion": "422"
  },
  "items": []
}
```

This is also propagated to the Swagger spec (which is how I noticed it, since I maintain the Rust bindings for the client API). v1.31.0:

```json
    "io.k8s.api.resource.v1alpha3.ResourceSliceList": {
        "listMeta": {
          "$ref": "#/definitions/io.k8s.apimachinery.pkg.apis.meta.v1.ListMeta",
          "description": "Standard list metadata"
        }
```

v1.30.3:

```json
    "io.k8s.api.resource.v1alpha2.ResourceSliceList": {
        "metadata": {
          "$ref": "#/definitions/io.k8s.apimachinery.pkg.apis.meta.v1.ListMeta",
          "description": "Standard list metadata"
        }
```

### What did you expect to happen?

As explained above.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Deploy v1.31.0 with `DynamicResourceAllocation` feature gate enabled and runtime config `resource.k8s.io/v1alpha3=true`. With kind, this is:

    ```yaml
    kind: Cluster
    apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
    featureGates:
      DynamicResourceAllocation: true
    runtimeConfig:
      'resource.k8s.io/v1alpha3': 'true'

issueContext.title: Code Generation Produces Ambiguous Fields and Duplicate Methods
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

The changes introduced in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121439 require that all types used with the generated clients implement both `runtime.Object` and `meta.Object`. In order to comply with this, we started embedding `metav1.ObjectMeta` in our API types that were missing it. However, we noticed that, for some of our types, the generator generates code with ambiguous fields and duplicate methods.

For example, consider the following case where both `metav1.ObjectMeta` and `MyEmbeddedType`, which are embedded in `MyType`, contain a `Namespace` field:

```
// +genclient
// +k8s:deepcopy-gen:interfaces=k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/runtime.Object

type MyType struct {
	metav1.TypeMeta   `json:",inline"`
	metav1.ObjectMeta `json:"metadata,omitempty"`

	MyEmbeddedType `json:"myEmbeddedType"`
}

type MyEmbeddedType struct {
	Namespace string `json:"namespace"`
}
```

This will generate code like:

```
func (b *MyTypeApplyConfiguration) WithNamespace(value string) *MyTypeApplyConfiguration {
	b.ensureObjectMetaApplyConfigurationExists()
	b.Namespace = &value
	return b
}
```

Here, `b.Namespace` is invalid because that field is present in both embedded types.



### What did you expect to happen?

Generator should be able to handle non-conflicting top-level fields.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

In this branch [1] I pushed 2 commits that will help visualize this issue better. Just pull it and run:

```
$ cd staging/src/k8s.io/sample-controller
$ go build -o sample-controller
# k8s.io/sample-controller/pkg/generated/applyconfiguration/samplecontroller/v1alpha1
pkg/generated/applyconfiguration/samplecontroller/v1alpha1/mytype.go:85:4: ambiguous selector b.Namespace
pkg/generated/applyconfiguration/samplecontroller/v1alpha1/mytype.go:207:36: method MyTypeApplyConfiguration.WithNamespace already declared at pkg/generated/applyconfiguration/samplecontroller/v

enrichment.problem: applyconfiguration-gen generated duplicate methods and ambiguous field accesses when a type embedded multiple structs that each defined a field with the same name (e.g., both metav1.ObjectMeta and a custom embedded struct had a Namespace field). The generated code referenced the ambiguous field directly, causing compilation errors.
enrichment.affected: API developers using applyconfiguration-gen, especially those with custom resources that embed metav1.ObjectMeta alongside other structs containing overlapping field names.
enrichment.fix: The generator was updated to detect name collisions among embedded struct members and stop generating duplicate setter methods or ambiguous member references. Conflicting fields are now omitted from the apply configuration struct, preventing invalid code.
enrichment.impact: Developers who rely on the applyconfiguration code generator for custom API types no longer encounter compile failures due to field name collisions, making server‑side apply code generation reliable and usable for a wider range of CRDs.

issueContext.body:
### What happened?

I created a kubernetes cluster with kubeadm and created a drop-in directory for kubelet configuration at `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d`.

I created a config file within the directory to change the value of `resolvConf`. After restarting kubelet, the value of `resolvConf` stayed same.

### What did you expect to happen?

The value of `resolvConf` is updated.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```sh
# Create custom resolv.conf
echo 'nameserver 8.8.8.8' | sudo tee /etc/resolv.kubelet.conf

# Create drop-in config directory
sudo mkdir /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d
sudo chmod 700 /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d

# Create drop-in config file
cat <<EOF | sudo tee /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d/99-resolv-conf.conf
apiVersion: kubelet.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: KubeletConfiguration
resolvConf: /etc/resolv.kubelet.conf
EOF
sudo chmod 600 /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d/99-resolv-conf.conf

# Add --config-dir flag
echo 'KUBELET_EXTRA_ARGS=--config-dir=/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d' | sudo tee /etc/default/kubelet

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl restart kubelet

# Check if the value of resolvConf is changed.
kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/<node name>/proxy/configz" | jq
```

### Anything else we need to know?

I think this issue is particular to the drop-in config and `resolvConf` option because:

- I can configure `resolvConf` by editing `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml`
- I can update another option like `streamingConnectionIdleTimeout` with drop-in config.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed the bug in `NodeUnschedulable` that only happens with QHint enabled, which the scheduler might miss some updates for the Pods rejected by NodeUnschedulable plugin and put the Pods in the queue for a longer time than needed.
bugOrRegression.author: sanposhiho
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange:
Fixes the bug in NodeUnschedulable that only happens with QHint enabled, 
which the scheduler might miss some updates for the Pods rejected by NodeUnschedulable plugin and put the Pods in the queue for a longer time than needed.

enrichment.problem: When the QHint (queue hint) feature is enabled, the NodeUnschedulable plugin can fail to propagate updates for Pods it rejects, causing the scheduler to keep those Pods in its queue longer than necessary.
enrichment.affected: Any workload whose Pods are rejected by the NodeUnschedulable plugin when QHint is enabled (e.g., Pods targeting unschedulable nodes).
enrichment.fix: The bug in the NodeUnschedulable plugin was corrected so that updates for rejected Pods are properly handled even with QHint enabled, allowing the scheduler to remove or re‑queue them promptly.
enrichment.impact: Pods that were previously delayed due to being stuck in the scheduler queue will now be rescheduled more quickly, reducing startup latency and improving overall scheduling efficiency.

enrichment.problem: When the scheduler's QueueHints (QHint) feature is enabled, the PodTopologySpread plugin could miss update events for Pods it rejects, causing those Pods to remain in the scheduling queue longer than necessary.
enrichment.affected: Any workloads with PodTopologySpread constraints running on clusters with QHint enabled; the scheduler may have delayed placement of those Pods.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler’s handling of QHint updates was corrected so that Pods rejected by the PodTopologySpread plugin are promptly removed from the queue and re‑evaluated, eliminating the unnecessary delay.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a bug where the scheduler didn't correctly tell plugins about Node deletion. This bug could impact all scheduler plugins subscribing to Node/Delete events, making the queue keep the Pods rejected by those plugins incorrectly at Node deletion. Among the in-tree plugins, PodTopologySpread is the only victim.
bugOrRegression.author: sanposhiho
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange:
Fixed a bug which the scheduler didn't correctly tell plugins Node deletion.
This bug could impact all scheduler plugins subscribing to Node/Delete event, making the queue keep the Pods rejected by those plugins incorrectly at Node deletion. Among the in-tree plugins, PodTopologySpread is the only victim.

enrichment.problem: The kube-scheduler failed to notify plugins of Node deletion events, causing plugins that subscribe to Node/Delete (e.g., PodTopologySpread) to retain pods in their rejection queues even after the node was removed.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using scheduler plugins that listen to Node/Delete events, specifically the in‑tree PodTopologySpread plugin, could see pods remain unschedulable after a node is deleted.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now correctly propagates Node deletion events to all registered plugins, allowing them to clear rejected pods from their queues when a node disappears.
enrichment.impact: Pods that were previously stuck in plugin rejection queues are now eligible for scheduling on remaining nodes, restoring proper pod placement and preventing potential scheduling dead‑locks for clusters using Node‑Delete‑aware plugins.

bugOrRegression.description: kubeadm: when adding new control plane nodes with `kubeadm join`, ensure that the etcd member addition is performed only if a given member URL does not already exist in the list of members. Similarly, on "kubeadm reset" only remove an etcd member if its ID exists.

bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: kubeadm: when adding new control plane nodes with "kubeamd join", ensure that the etcd member addition is performed only if a given member URL does not already exist in the list of members. Similarly, on "kubeadm reset" only remove an etcd member if its ID exists.

enrichment.problem: When adding a new control‑plane node with `kubeadm join`, kubeadm could attempt to add an etcd member even if that member URL already existed, and `kubeadm reset` could try to remove an etcd member whose ID was not present, leading to errors or inconsistent etcd membership.
enrichment.affected: Users adding or removing control‑plane nodes with `kubeadm join` and `kubeadm reset`. Scenarios where the same etcd member URL or ID might already be present.
enrichment.fix: The join flow now checks the existing etcd member list and adds a member only if its URL is not already present. The reset flow now checks for the member ID before attempting removal, skipping the operation if the ID does not exist.
enrichment.impact: Idempotent `kubeadm join` and `kubeadm reset` operations prevent spurious failures when re‑running these commands, making control‑plane provisioning and teardown more reliable.

bugOrRegression.description: DRA: when enabling the scheduler queuing hint feature, pods got stuck as unschedulable for a while unnecessarily because recording the name of the generated ResourceClaim did not trigger scheduling.
bugOrRegression.author: pohly

enrichment.problem: When the scheduler queuing hint feature was enabled, pods that used Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) remained in an unschedulable state because recording the name of the generated ResourceClaim did not trigger a rescheduling attempt.
enrichment.affected: Workloads that enable the scheduler queuing hint feature and use Dynamic Resource Allocation (ResourceClaims). These pods could remain pending indefinitely until the issue was fixed.
enrichment.fix: The scheduling logic was updated so that recording the generated ResourceClaim name now correctly triggers the scheduler to re‑evaluate the pod, allowing it to be placed once the claim is ready.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on DRA no longer get stuck unschedulable, reducing scheduling delays and preventing unnecessary pod failures for workloads that enable the queuing hint feature.

issueContext.title: During the deployment of Kubernetes 1.31.0 and MultiCIDRServiceAllocator was enabled, which then led to a failure when creating a service.
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

When deploying Kubernetes 1.31.0 with MultiCIDRServiceAllocator enabled, an error occurs when trying to create a service in the cluster with the following error message:

```bash
root@controller-node-1:~# kubectl apply -f test-service.yaml
Error from server (InternalError): error when creating "test-service.yaml": Internal error occurred: failed to allocate a serviceIP: range is full
```

Am I missing some necessary configuration? Can you help me take a look?  Thanks.

### What did you expect to happen?

Can successfully create a service

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Deploy k8s and enable the featureGate MultiCIDRServiceAllocator function
2. Then create a service and enable IPv6
3. The service yaml information for the test is as follows:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: dual-stack-service
  namespace: default
spec:
  ipFamilyPolicy: RequireDualStack
  ipFamilies:
    - IPv4
    - IPv6
  selector:
    app: my-app
  ports:
    - name: http
      protocol: TCP
      port: 80
      targetPort: 80
  type: ClusterIP
```

4. Disable MultiCIDRServiceAllocator feature, create with same service yaml, everything works fine.

```bash
kubectl apply -f test.yaml             
service/dual-stack-service created
```

### Anything else we need to know?

Check kube-apiserver and you will see the following error

```

enrichment.problem: When MultiCIDRServiceAllocator beta feature is enabled in dual‑stack clusters, creating Services that require dual‑stack IPs or IPs from the secondary range fails with an allocation error ("range is full").
enrichment.affected: Clusters with dual‑stack networking that have the MultiCIDRServiceAllocator feature enabled; Service creation would fail.
enrichment.fix: The bug in the service IP allocator was fixed, allowing MultiCIDRServiceAllocator to correctly allocate primary and secondary IPs for dual‑stack Services. A temporary workaround is to disable the dual‑write path by setting the feature gate DisableAllocatorDualWrite=true.

bugOrRegression.author: danwinship

Fixes a regression introduced in 1.29 where conntrack entries for UDP connections

issueContext.title: Conntrack tables having stale entries for UDP connection
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

We experienced an EC2 node failure within our EKS cluster. This affected node was running two CoreDNS pods, which are responsible for DNS resolution in our Kubernetes cluster. Envoy connects to CoreDNS through the UDP protocol. After these CoreDNS pods were terminated, Envoy continued to attempt connections to the terminated IP for DNS resolution.
The kube-proxy failed to update the entry in the conntrack tables, causing some Envoy pods to still connect to the terminated CoreDNS pod IP. Once we restarted the Envoy pods, the entry was refreshed, and the DNS timeout issue was resolved.

Mapping in Conntrack table for src pod ip-10.103.83.53 for UDP protocol.

Query : “conntrack -p udp -L --src 10.103.83.53”

Response : “udp  17 27 src=10.103.83.53 dst=<clusterIp> sport=21667 dport=53 [UNREPLIED] src=10.103.78.37 dst=10.103.83.53 sport=53 dport=21667 mark=0 use=1 contrack v1.4.4 (conntrack-tools): 1 flow entries have been shown”

### What did you expect to happen?

Kubeproxy should update or refresh this conntrack table. 
conntrack shouldn't have stale UDP connection routes.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

KubeProxy version we tested with - kube-proxy:v1.29.4-minimal-eksbuild.1

which include this fix as well -  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119249

Steps we followed in our EKS cluster to stimulate this issue

- Remove podAntiAffinity on the coreDNS deployment
- Identify the node where we would want to concentrate the coreDNS to cordon it
- Evict workloads from that node
- Make that for not getting scaled down using node annotations
- Uncordon that node, and cordon the rest of the node
- Delete two coreDNS pods
- Ensure they get scheduled to that targeted node
- Login to that node, install tmux, and down all the network interfaces to simulate the 2/2 failure
- Notice the node going into NotReady state, and check for the DNS c-ares errors

Resource Requests = Max ( Max( each InitContainerUse ) , Sum(Sidecar Containers) + Sum(Containers) )

enrichment.problem: The kube-scheduler calculated a pod's total resource requests using only regular containers and init containers, ignoring the resource requests of sidecar containers. This could lead to pods being scheduled onto nodes without sufficient resources for their sidecars, causing resource contention or pod failures.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that defines sidecar containers with resource requests, such as logging agents, service mesh proxies, or sidecar‑based side processes, could have been scheduled incorrectly.
enrichment.fix: Scheduler logic was updated to include the summed resource requests of sidecar containers when scoring a pod. The calculation now follows the KEP‑753 model: max(max init container request, sum(sidecar requests) + sum(main container requests)).
enrichment.impact: Pods that include sidecar containers will be scheduled based on their true total resource needs, preventing over‑commitment of node resources and reducing the likelihood of runtime failures or node pressure. This improves reliability for workloads that rely on sidecars for logging, monitoring, or proxying.

issueContext.title: Named ports specified in sidecar container pod spec are not available to services
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

When migrating a sidecar container to a native sidecar container (initContainer with restartPolicy=Always), traffic going via the Kubernetes Service did not reach the application container/sidecar container.

### What did you expect to happen?

The traffic should have reached the sidecar container like before the migration.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a Pod with a native sidecar container (initContainer) with a named port, as well as a Kubernetes Service using that named port as its targetPort. This port is not listed in the Endpoint.

Apply the following:

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: sidecar-ports
  labels:
    app: sidecar-ports
spec:
  containers:
  - image: bloomberg/goldpinger:3.10.1
    name: goldpinger
    ports:
    - containerPort: 8000
      name: http
      protocol: TCP
  initContainers:
  # note: no envoy configuration is provided, the steps to reproduce involve reading other Kubernetes manifests (Endpoints)
  - image: envoyproxy/envoy:v1.73.7
    name: tls-terminator
    ports:
    - containerPort: 9443
      name: https
      protocol: TCP
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: sidecar-ports
spec:
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 80
    protocol: TCP
    targetPort: http
  - name: https
    port: 443
    protocol: TCP
    targetPort: https
  selector:
    app: sidecar-ports
  type: ClusterIP
```

The Endpoint backing the created Service "sidecar-ports" should contain two ports; "http" and "https", but it only contains "http":
```
k describe endpoints sidecar-ports
Name:         sidecar-ports
Namespace:    default
Subsets:
  Ports:
    Name  Port  Protocol
    ----  ----  --------
    http  8000  TCP

Events:  <none>
```

### Anything else we need to know?

The feature gate is enabled:

```
kubectl get --raw /metrics | grep kubernetes_feature_enabled | grep SidecarContainers

enrichment.problem: When a pod defines a native sidecar container (initContainer with restartPolicy=Always) that exposes a named port, that named port is omitted from the pod's Endpoint objects. Consequently, a Service targeting the named port via targetPort cannot route traffic to the sidecar container.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use native sidecar (initContainer) containers with named ports, and any Service that targets those ports by name. Users migrating sidecar patterns are impacted.
enrichment.fix: The endpoint controller now includes named ports from sidecar (init) containers when constructing Endpoint subsets, making those ports visible to Services that reference them by name.
enrichment.impact: Services can correctly route traffic to sidecar containers using named ports, fixing breakage that occurred after migrating sidecars to native initContainers. This restores expected traffic flow for workloads that rely on sidecars for proxying, TLS termination, etc.

issueContext.title: Restore build-tag flag for code-generator

### What happened?

The `build-tag` flag is removed in 1.30 as code-generator moved to use `gengo/v2` and removed `gengo/args` dependency where `GeneratedBuildTag` arg resides. As a result, it is not possible to inject a custom build tag during `conversion-gen` and `defaulter-gen` process.

This flag is useful for other projects that need a custom tag to differentiate itself from the default build tag of `gengo` which is `ignore_autogenerated`. By using a custom build tag that is different from the default build tag, those two files can be used during `conversion-gen` and `defaulter-gen` processes.

[2] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/apis/core/v1/zz_generated.defaults.go

### What did you expect to happen?

The `build-tag` flag shouldn't be deprecated prematurely as it is still useful to inject a custom build tag.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a bug where `podCIDR` was released before the node was deleted.

issueContext.title: kube-controller-manager re-allocating already used PodCIDR (v1.31)
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

Since upgrading to Kubernetes v1.31 we have occasional observed that `kube-controller-manager` allocates a PodCIDR for a new node which is already allocated for an existing node in the cluster. We have about 200 clusters with a combined number of ca. 6k-10k nodes (autoscaling). It has happened about 10 times since upgrading a week ago, so it's rather rare but breaks the networking between the affected nodes when it happens.

We use flannel as overlay network and it uses the podCIDR assigned by `kube-controller-manager`. When a new node gets an existing podCIDR assigned, then the new node doesn't get ready and it gets terminated after 10 min. We check that the node is routable by all other nodes before we mark the node ready. This never happens because the podCIDR already points to another node in the cluster. When the new node is deleted it has the very unfortunate side effect that all flannels detect the node is deleted and they delete the routes for the podCIDR, problem is just that most nodes will have routes for the other node with the same podCIDR and this then stops working.

Terminating the affected node is the best way to resolve the issue but obviously not sustainable.

### What did you expect to happen?

`kube-controller-manager` should _never_ allocate the same podCIDR to multiple nodes at the same time.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

We haven't found a predictable way to reproduce it.

We run with the pod CIDR range: `10.2.0.0/15`.

### Anything else we need to know?

This is how we configure `kube-controller-manager`: https://github.com/zalando-incubator/kubernetes-on-aws/blob/dev/cluster/node-pools/master-default/userdata.yaml#L581-L648 (the image is vanilla Kubernetes built from source and hosted in a private registry)

Here is an example from one cluster with logs:

*Node 1 (original)*:
name: `ip-172-31-14-210.eu-central-1.compute.internal`
podCIDR: `10.2.4.0/24`

enrichment.problem: kube-controller-manager released a node's podCIDR before the node was fully deleted, allowing the same podCIDR to be re‑allocated to a new node. This caused duplicate CIDR usage, breaking overlay network routing (e.g., flannel) and preventing the new node from becoming Ready.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that run kube-controller-manager and use podCIDR‑based overlay networking (e.g., flannel). Nodes being deleted or replaced could experience CIDR conflicts and networking outages.
enrichment.fix: Changed the node deletion flow in kube-controller-manager so that podCIDR release is deferred until after the node object is fully removed, preventing premature reuse of the CIDR block.
enrichment.impact: Eliminates duplicate PodCIDR assignments, restoring correct network connectivity for newly added nodes and avoiding node‑readiness failures. Improves cluster stability for clusters that frequently add/remove nodes, especially those using flannel or similar overlay networks.

enrichment.problem: During CoreDNS cache updates, the cache plugin could emit both successful and denial responses, leading to conflicting DNS answers (e.g., NXDOMAIN vs NOERROR). This caused flaky name resolution for headless services and delayed publishing of pod IPs for statefulsets, manifesting as long startup pauses and intermittent DNS failures.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters provisioned with kubeadm that run CoreDNS with the cache plugin. Affected workloads include pods, headless services, and statefulsets that depend on DNS for service discovery.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now adds two new cache plugin parameters – "disable success" and "disable denial" – to the Corefile it generates. Enabling these flags stops the cache from returning contradictory success and denial responses, ensuring consistent DNS answers after cache updates.
enrichment.impact: DNS resolution becomes reliable and fast, eliminating the ~30‑second delay for pod name availability and preventing intermittent lookup failures. Clusters that use kubeadm‑managed CoreDNS with the cache plugin—especially those with headless services or statefulsets relying on DNS for peer discovery—will see more stable pod communication and quicker application start‑up.

issueContext.title: 1.32.0-rc.0 kubelet fails to mount volumes from windows GCEPD CSI driver
issueContext.body:
A downstream e2e test creating / attaching / mounting / writing to a GCE PD CSI volume is working on latest 1.31 releases and failing with a 1.32.0-rc.0 kubelet. Nothing else changed between the passing and failing run (same OS level, same versions of all other components including CSI driver,  etc).

Bisected to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127076, when kubelet started being built with go 1.23.

[Many things changed in go 1.23 around filesystem handing](https://tip.golang.org/doc/go1.23#ospkgos), and it doesn't look like kubelet volume code reacted to those.

Building the kubelet with `winsymlink=0` resolved the issue.

> On Windows, the mode bits reported by [Lstat](https://tip.golang.org/pkg/os#Lstat) and [Stat](https://tip.golang.org/pkg/os#Stat) for reparse points changed. Mount points no longer have [ModeSymlink](https://tip.golang.org/pkg/os#ModeSymlink) set, and reparse points that are not symlinks, Unix sockets, or dedup files now always have [ModeIrregular](https://tip.golang.org/pkg/os#ModeIrregular) set. This behavior is controlled by the winsymlink setting. For Go 1.23, it defaults to winsymlink=1. Previous versions default to winsymlink=0.

> On Windows, [EvalSymlinks](https://tip.golang.org/pkg/path/filepath#EvalSymlinks) no longer evaluates mount points, which was a source of many inconsistencies and bugs. This behavior is controlled by the winsymlink setting. For Go 1.23, it defaults to winsymlink=1. Previous versions default to winsymlink=0.

There are other stdlib windows fs behavior changes as well:

> On Windows, Readlink no longer tries to normalize volumes to drive letters, which was not always even possible. This behavior is controlled by the winreadlinkvolume setting. For Go 1.23, it defaults to winreadlinkvolume=1. Previous versions default to winreadlinkvolume=0.

> On Windows, EvalSymlinks no longer tries to normalize volumes to drive letters, which was not always even possible. This behavior is controlled

enrichment.problem: Kubelet on Windows nodes fails to mount CSI volumes (e.g., GCE PD) after being built with Go 1.23, because the new default winsymlink=1 changes how reparse points and mount points are reported, breaking the mount logic.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running Windows nodes that rely on CSI drivers (e.g., GCE PD) experienced volume mount failures, affecting any pods that needed persistent storage.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet is built with winsymlink=0 (or adjusted code) so that Windows filesystem handling matches prior Go behavior, allowing CSI volume mount operations to succeed.
enrichment.impact: Stateful workloads on Windows nodes can again attach and use CSI storage, preventing pod start failures and restoring full functionality for Windows clusters upgraded to 1.32.0 release candidates.

issueContext.title: [scheduler] Remove deprecated EBS/GCE/Azure/Cinder predicates
issueContext.body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

/sig scheduling
/priority important-longterm
/assign

We should remove the EBS/GCE/Azure/Cinder predicates from scheduler after CSIMigration goes GA (probably in 1.18).

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8c537b46939beed3713356f71449a8ad6829b725/pkg/scheduler/algorithm/predicates/predicates.go#L80-L95

> Since we are in process of migrating in-tree volume plugins to CSI, there is already a CSI predicate available which handles all volume plugins and hence when using CSI volumes - the cloudprovider specific predicates are not required. We will be able to truly remove these predicates once CSI migration goes GA but we will have a translation layer as well, which would take care of handling in-tree volume plugins even if you are not using CSI. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/74544#issuecomment-467531169

#### Reference

+ https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/74544#issuecomment-467531169
+ https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/625

enrichment.problem: The kube-scheduler plugins AzureDiskLimits, CinderLimits, EBSLimits, and GCEPDLimits were deprecated. If they are explicitly enabled in a scheduler configuration, the scheduler will fail to load them, causing scheduling errors for workloads that rely on volume limit predicates.
enrichment.affected: Administrators who have custom kube-scheduler configurations that explicitly enable AzureDiskLimits, CinderLimits, EBSLimits, or GCEPDLimits plugins.
enrichment.fix: The plugins have been removed from the scheduler code. Scheduler now obtains per‑node volume limits from the CSINode object populated by kubelet (which receives the limits from the CSI driver’s NodeGetInfoResponse). Users must delete any references to these plugins from their scheduler configuration.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that manually enable any of the removed limit plugins will need to update their scheduler config; otherwise the scheduler will reject the configuration and pods may remain unscheduled. After the change, volume limit information is automatically provided via CSI, simplifying configuration and improving compatibility with CSI drivers.

issueContext.title: Passing CDI devices as annotations should be removed
issueContext.body:
Kubelet should stop using annotations to pass CDI device IDs to CRI runtimes. CDIDevices CRI field should be used for this purpose.

This should be done when Kubelet that doesn't support CRI field reaches EOL and two major CRI runtimes support CRI field.

Here is a PR comment that gives more details about this: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/115891/files#r1112169121

- Kubelet started using CDIDevices CRI field in [v1.28.0](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.28.md#api-change-2). Previous version 1.27 will reach EOL [2024-06-28](https://kubernetes.io/releases/patch-releases/#1-27).

- CRI-O started using it in [v1.28.0](https://github.com/cri-o/cri-o/releases/tag/v1.28.0). Previous version 1.27 will reach EOL [2024-06-28](https://kubernetes.io/releases/patch-releases/#1-27) together with Kubernetes 1.27.

- Containerd started using it in [1.7.2](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v1.7.2). Version 1.7 will reach EOL in a 6 months after Containerd 2.0 release https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/main/RELEASES.md. Previous version 1.6 doesn't support CDI injections and should not be considered.

So, safer option would be to wait until Containerd 1.7 reaches EOL. However it's relatively safe to do it earlier when 1.7.0 and 1.7.1 have little chances to be in real use.

Containerd v1.7.0 and v1.7.1 is not used by the Linux distributions from [this long list](https://pkgs.org/search/?q=containerd), so it's safe to remove annotations support from the Kubelet in 1.31 in my opinion.

enrichment.problem: Kubelet was passing CDI device IDs to container runtimes via pod annotations. Older containerd versions (< v1.7.2) do not understand the newer CDIDevices CRI field, so they cannot receive the device information, leading to missing devices for workloads that rely on CDI.
enrichment.affected: Pods that request CDI devices on nodes where kubelet 1.28+ runs with containerd versions older than 1.7.2.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet stops using annotations and instead populates the CDIDevices field in the CRI Device plugin request. Nodes running containerd must be upgraded to v1.7.2 or newer to accept the CDI information.
enrichment.impact: Workloads that depend on CDI devices (e.g., GPUs, FPGAs) will work only on nodes with containerd ≥ 1.7.2. Users with older containerd versions need to upgrade to avoid device injection failures.

other.description: kube-proxy now reconciles Service/Endpoint changes with conntrack table and cleans up only stale UDP flow entries
other.author: aroradaman

issueContext.title: Implement a kube-proxy conntrack reconciler
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

We'd like to have conntrack reconciler for Services in kube-proxy, for each Service or Endpoint change it should reconcile the Service/Endpoint table with the existing conntrack table and remove stale UDP entries (we have concluded in other issues that UDP is the only protocol that requires this)

### Why is this needed?

Despite a lot of work and testing was added to solve the problem with stale UDP entries that can blackhole traffic, we still have reports of issues related to UDP stale entries

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/125467

Also, the conntrack logic is event based and, as expected, if something fails it never reconciles

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/112604

The reconciler will only delete the entries that are known to be stale, other entries will time out.

### References

Some WIP I had https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/compare/master...aojea:kubernetes:conntrack_done_right?expand=1

### Related issues that will be fixed

- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/125979
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/125467
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/122740

enrichment.problem: Stale UDP conntrack entries were not being removed when Services or Endpoints changed, causing UDP traffic to be blackholed. The existing event‑based reconciler could miss failures and never clean up these entries.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that relies on UDP Services, across Linux and Windows nodes, was at risk of lost packets due to stale conntrack entries.
enrichment.fix: kube-proxy now runs a conntrack reconciler on every Service/Endpoint change. It compares the current Service/Endpoint table with the conntrack table and deletes only the stale UDP flow entries, leaving other entries to expire naturally.
enrichment.impact: UDP‑based services (e.g., DNS, media streaming, telemetry) regain reliable traffic handling. Clusters on both Linux and Windows no longer experience intermittent UDP blackholes, improving overall service stability.

enrichment.problem: Admission control configuration files passed via --admission-control-config-file were parsed leniently, allowing duplicate or unknown fields to be silently ignored, leading to potential misconfiguration.
