enrichment.fix: The API server now validates these configuration files in strict mode (EnableStrict). Any duplicate or unknown fields cause the apiserver to reject the file with an error.
enrichment.impact: Users get immediate feedback on invalid admission configuration, preventing silent misconfigurations that could weaken cluster security or cause unexpected admission behavior.

other.description: The getters for the field name and typeDescription of the Reflector struct have been renamed.
other.author: alexanderstephan
other.userFacingChange: The getters for the field name and typeDescription of the Reflector struct were renamed.

enrichment.problem: The getter method names for the Reflector struct's fields 'name' and 'typeDescription' did not follow the standard naming convention, causing inconsistency and potential compile errors for callers using the old names.
enrichment.affected: Any Go code or component that directly called the old Reflector getter methods, such as custom controllers, client-go users, or core components that embed Reflector (e.g., controller-manager, scheduler).
enrichment.fix: The getter methods have been renamed to match standard naming (e.g., Name() and TypeDescription()) instead of the previous GetName() and GetTypeDescription().
enrichment.impact: Code that referenced the old getter names will no longer compile until updated to the new method names. No runtime behavior change for clusters that are rebuilt with the updated code.

other.description: kube-apiserver `ResourceQuotaConfiguration` admission plugin subsection within `--admission-control-config-file` files is now validated strictly (EnableStrict). Duplicate and unknown fields in the configuration will now cause errors.
other.author: seans3
other.userFacingChange: kube-apiserver ResourceQuotaConfiguration admission plugin subsection within `--admission-control-config-file` files are now validated strictly (EnableStrict). Duplicate and unknown fields in the configuration will now cause an error.

enrichment.problem: Admission control config files for the ResourceQuotaConfiguration plugin were previously validated leniently, allowing duplicate or unknown fields to be silently ignored, which could lead to misconfigurations and unexpected behavior.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the ResourceQuotaConfiguration admission plugin via `--admission-control-config-file`. Specifically, admins with configs containing duplicate or unknown fields will encounter startup errors.
enrichment.fix: The kube-apiserver now validates the ResourceQuotaConfiguration subsection in `--admission-control-config-file` strictly (EnableStrict). Any duplicate or unknown fields now cause the apiserver to reject the configuration with an error.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators will get immediate feedback on invalid admission plugin configurations, preventing hard‑to‑debug quota enforcement issues. Configs that relied on non‑strict validation must be corrected before upgrading.

other.description: CRI client now uses the default timeout for `ImageFsInfo` RPC.
other.author: saschagrunert
other.userFacingChange: CRI client: use default timeout for `ImageFsInfo` RPC

enrichment.problem: The CRI client used a custom (short) timeout for the ImageFsInfo RPC instead of the default timeout, causing the call to fail or be aborted on nodes where gathering image filesystem information took longer, potentially leading to inaccurate node status or reduced reliability.
enrichment.affected: Kubelet on nodes that query image filesystem information via the CRI; workloads are unaffected directly but node health reporting may improve.
enrichment.fix: The CRI client now respects the default timeout for the ImageFsInfo RPC, allowing the call to complete within the expected time window.
enrichment.impact: Improves kubelet stability on nodes with large image caches or slow storage, preventing spurious errors and ensuring accurate reporting of image filesystem usage.

other.description: The kube-apiserver `--tracing-config-file` is now validated strictly (EnableStrict). Duplicate and unknown fields in the configuration will now result in an error.
other.author: seans3
other.userFacingChange: kube-apiserver `--tracing-config-file` file is now validated strictly (EnableStrict). Duplicate and unknown fields in the configuration will now cause an error.

enrichment.problem: The kube-apiserver did not strictly validate the tracing configuration file, allowing duplicate or unknown fields to be silently ignored, leading to misconfigured tracing.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running kube-apiserver with a custom `--tracing-config-file`; setups that had duplicate or unknown fields in the tracing config will see startup errors.
enrichment.fix: Enable strict validation (EnableStrict) for the `--tracing-config-file` option so that any duplicate or unknown fields cause the apiserver to reject the config with an error.
enrichment.impact: Users get immediate feedback on invalid tracing configs, preventing silent misconfiguration and ensuring observability works as intended. Misconfigured APIs will now fail fast instead of running with partial tracing.

other.description: Fixed spacing in `--validate flag` description in kubectl.
other.author: soltysh
other.userFacingChange: Fix spacing in --validate flag description in kubectl.

enrichment.problem: The help text for the `--validate` flag in kubectl had incorrect spacing, making the description unclear.
enrichment.affected: Anyone using `kubectl` and reviewing the `--validate` flag description via help commands.
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the spacing in the `--validate` flag description so the help output is formatted correctly.
enrichment.impact: Users see a clearer, more readable help message for the `--validate` flag, improving command‑line usability.

other.description: Updated cni-plugins to [v1.6.0](https://github.com/containernetworking/plugins/releases/tag/v1.6.0).
other.author: saschagrunert

enrichment.problem: Not specified
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes nodes that run the CNI plugin for pod networking (via kubelet).
enrichment.fix: The CNI plugins used for pod networking are upgraded to version v1.6.0, bringing in upstream bug fixes, performance improvements, and new features.
enrichment.impact: Clusters will use the newer CNI plugin binaries, which can improve network stability, security, and functionality for pod networking.

other.description: Clarified an API validation error for toleration if `operator` is `Exists` and `value` is not empty.
other.author: saschagrunert

enrichment.problem: When a toleration is defined with operator `Exists` and a non‑empty `value`, the API server returned a generic validation error that was unclear to users.
enrichment.affected: Anyone who defines pod tolerations—e.g., via Pod, Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet manifests—when mistakenly sets a non‑empty `value` with `operator: Exists`.
enrichment.fix: The validation error message has been updated to explicitly state that `value` must be empty when `operator` is `Exists`, providing clearer guidance.
enrichment.impact: Users creating or updating Pods (or higher‑level workload objects) will see a precise error, making it easier to correct invalid toleration specifications.

other.description: Feature `AllowServiceLBStatusOnNonLB` remains deprecated and is now locked to false to ensure compatibility with previous versions.
other.author: Jefftree
other.userFacingChange: Feature `AllowServiceLBStatusOnNonLB` remains deprecated and is now locked to false to support compatibility versions

enrichment.problem: The feature gate AllowServiceLBStatusOnNonLB could be enabled, leading to incompatibilities with older Kubernetes versions that do not support LoadBalancer status on non‑LoadBalancer services.
enrichment.affected: Users who enabled the AllowServiceLBStatusOnNonLB feature gate, and any workloads relying on Service load‑balancer status for non‑LoadBalancer services.
enrichment.fix: The feature gate is now locked to false (cannot be enabled) while remaining deprecated, ensuring clusters stay compatible with previous version behavior.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can no longer opt‑in to this feature, preventing potential runtime errors or version skew. Existing workloads are unaffected, but users who had the gate enabled must disable it.

other.description: Vendor: updated system-validators to v1.9.0.
other.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: Existing system-validators had bugs or missing checks that could cause nodes to be incorrectly validated or reject valid configurations, leading to node registration or runtime issues.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where nodes use the system-validators for node validation, particularly during kubelet startup and node registration.
enrichment.fix: Updates the system-validators component to v1.9.0, which includes corrected validation logic and additional checks, improving reliability of node system validation during cluster lifecycle.
enrichment.impact: Ensures nodes are properly validated and can join the cluster without spurious failures, reducing downtime and improving stability for workloads running on those nodes.

other.description: Fixed a bug in the `k8s.io/cloud-provider/service` controller, which may panic when a service is updated because the event recorder was used before it was initialized. All cloud providers using the `v1.31.0` cloud provider service controller must ensure that the controller is initialized before the informer starts to process events or update it to version 1.32.0.
other.author: carlory
other.userFacingChange: Fixes a bug in the `k8s.io/cloud-provider/service`  controller, it may panic when a service is updated because the event recorder was used before it was initialized. All cloud providers should using the `v1.31.0` cloud provider service controller must ensure that the controllers is initialized before the informer start to process events or update it to the version 1.32.0.

issueContext.title: Crash on kube manager's service-lb-controller after v1.31.0
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

If kube manager is started with no `cloud-provider`, it looks like the service-lb-controller is instantiated but not started. However, part of its initialization happens on the `Run` method **and** its handlers are added to the informer on instantiation. So the handlers still run and it crashes when they do because there is stuff not initialized, like in this case, the event recorder:
```2024-10-14T11:27:20.573127782Z stderr F 	goroutine 735 [running]:
2024-10-14T11:27:20.573132561Z stderr F 	k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime.logPanic({0x38432a0, 0x5545b00}, {0x2d99000, 0x5480790})
2024-10-14T11:27:20.573137951Z stderr F 		k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime/runtime.go:107 +0xbc
2024-10-14T11:27:20.573154772Z stderr F 	k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime.handleCrash({0x38432a0, 0x5545b00}, {0x2d99000, 0x5480790}, {0x5545b00, 0x0, 0x43d945?})
2024-10-14T11:27:20.573159501Z stderr F 		k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime/runtime.go:82 +0x5e
2024-10-14T11:27:20.573187343Z stderr F 	k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime.HandleCrash({0x0, 0x0, 0xc001e5ec40?})
2024-10-14T11:27:20.573192182Z stderr F 		k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime/runtime.go:59 +0x108
2024-10-14T11:27:20.57319655Z stderr F 	panic({0x2d99000?, 0x5480790?})
2024-10-14T11:27:20.573200548Z stderr F 		runtime/panic.go:770 +0x132
2024-10-14T11:27:20.573204836Z stderr F 	k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service.(*Controller).needsUpdate(0xc000978000, 0xc00324c288, 0xc000cf3688)
2024-10-14T11:27:20.573210016Z stderr F 		k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go:606 +0xcbb
2024-10-14T11:27:20.573214644Z stderr F 	k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service.New.func2({0x326c8e0?, 0xc00324c288?}, {0x326c8e0, 0xc000cf3688?})
2024-10-14T11:27:20.573219133Z stderr F 		k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go:144 +0x74

2024-10-14T11:27:20.

enrichment.problem: The cloud-provider service controller (service‑lb‑controller) could panic on a service update because it attempted to use the event recorder before it was initialized, causing the kube‑controller‑manager to crash.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters that run the v1.31.0 cloud‑provider service controller (the service‑lb‑controller) – typically any cloud‑provider integration that updates Services.
enrichment.fix: The controller now guarantees that its initialization (including the event recorder) completes before the informer starts handling events. Clusters should either upgrade to the v1.32.0 controller where this guard is added, or manually ensure the controller is fully initialized before the informer begins processing.
enrichment.impact: Prevents controller‑manager crashes and loss of service load‑balancer functionality for clusters using the v1.31.0 cloud‑provider service controller, improving overall stability and uptime.

other.description: Removed legacy cloud provider integration code and the "service-lb-controller", "cloud-node-lifecycle-controller" and the "node-route-controller" from kube-controller-manager. You can now either set the `--cloud-provider` command line argument to "external", or to the empty string. All other values are invalid.
other.author: aojea

enrichment.problem: Legacy in‑tree cloud provider integration code and the service‑lb‑controller, cloud‑node‑lifecycle‑controller, and node‑route‑controller were removed from kube‑controller‑manager. Clusters that still set --cloud-provider to a non‑empty, non‑"external" value now encounter invalid configuration errors.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that relied on in‑tree cloud provider controllers (service load balancer, node lifecycle, and node routes) and any configuration using --cloud-provider with a non‑external value.
enrichment.fix: The removed controllers are no longer compiled. Users must set the --cloud-provider flag to "external" or an empty string. All other values are rejected, prompting migration to the external cloud‑provider model.
enrichment.impact: Encourages migration to the external cloud‑provider architecture, removes deprecated code paths, and prevents accidental use of unsupported cloud‑provider settings, simplifying the controller‑manager and improving maintainability.

other.description: `ComponentSLIs` feature is marked as GA and locked.
other.author: Jefftree

enrichment.problem: ComponentSLIs were only in an early stage (alpha/beta) and not officially supported, limiting their use in production and causing uncertainty for users needing stable SLI metrics.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that consume ComponentSLI metrics for monitoring, alerting, or SLO calculations. Existing users gain stability; new users can adopt the feature safely.
enrichment.fix: The ComponentSLIs feature is promoted to General Availability (GA) and locked, meaning the API and semantics are now stable and no further incompatible changes will be made.
enrichment.impact: Users can now rely on ComponentSLI metrics in production environments with confidence that the feature is fully supported and will not change unexpectedly, improving observability and SLO tracking.

other.description: The `dynamicResources` has been refactored to `DynamicResources`, now users can introduce the `DynamicResources` struct outside the `dynamicresources` package.
other.author: JesseStutler

enrichment.problem: The `dynamicResources` struct was unexported and confined to the `dynamicresources` package, preventing users from defining or extending it outside that package.
enrichment.affected: Developers building custom node or scheduler plugins, and any workload relying on dynamic resource definitions.
enrichment.fix: Refactored the type to an exported `DynamicResources` struct and moved it out of the `dynamicresources` package, allowing external code to instantiate and use the struct directly.
enrichment.impact: Enables custom implementations and extensions that rely on dynamic resource definitions, improving flexibility for node and scheduling developers and simplifying integration with custom plugins.

other.description: Added a health check for the device plugin gRPC registration server. When the registration server is down, kubelet is marked as unhealthy. If systemd watchdog is configured, this will result in a kubelet restart.
other.author: zhifei92

enrichment.problem: Kubelet did not monitor the health of the device plugin gRPC registration server, so if the registration server went down the node could remain in a degraded state without alerting the system.
enrichment.affected: Nodes using device plugin gRPC registration servers, especially those with systemd watchdog enabled, and any pods that rely on those device plugins.
enrichment.fix: A health check is added for the device plugin registration server. When the server is unavailable, kubelet reports itself as unhealthy, which triggers a systemd watchdog‑initiated restart if one is configured.
enrichment.impact: Improves node reliability for workloads that depend on device plugins (e.g., GPUs, NICs). Nodes will automatically recover from registration server failures, reducing manual intervention and preventing hidden node issues.

other.description: kubeadm: consider --bind-address or --advertise-address and --secure-port for control plane components when the feature gate WaitForAllControlPlaneComponents is enabled. Use /livez for kube-apiserver and kube-scheduler, but continue using /healthz for kube-controller-manager until it supports /livez.
other.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: When the WaitForAllControlPlaneComponents feature gate was enabled, kubeadm ignored the --bind-address/--advertise-address and --secure-port flags for control plane components, and it used inconsistent health endpoints, leading to potential startup and health‑check failures for the API server and scheduler.
enrichment.affected: Users enabling the WaitForAllControlPlaneComponents feature gate via kubeadm; control‑plane components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager) that rely on correct address/port settings and health checks.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now respects the specified bind/advertise address and secure port flags for control‑plane components under the WaitForAllControlPlaneComponents gate. It also switches to using the /livez endpoint for kube-apiserver and kube-scheduler health probes, while keeping /healthz for kube-controller-manager until it supports /livez.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that enable the WaitForAllControlPlaneComponents feature gate will have correct binding and port configuration for control‑plane components and more reliable liveness probing, reducing start‑up failures and improving cluster stability.

other.description: CBOR-encoded watch responses now set the Content-Type header to "application/cbor-seq" instead of the nonconformant "application/cbor".
other.author: benluddy

enrichment.problem: Watch responses encoded in CBOR were sent with the non‑standard Content‑Type header "application/cbor" instead of the correct media type "application/cbor-seq", causing clients that rely on proper content‑type negotiation to reject or mis‑parse the watch stream.
enrichment.affected: Clients using the watch API with CBOR encoding and the kube‑apiserver that serves those responses.
enrichment.fix: The kube‑apiserver now sets the Content‑Type header for CBOR‑encoded watch responses to the conformant "application/cbor-seq" media type.
enrichment.impact: Ensures compatibility with clients that consume CBOR watch streams, aligns the API with the official specification, and prevents errors when parsing watch data.

other.description: Enabled `CBORServingAndStorage` feature gate – built-in APIs can now be served in CBOR format for clients that request it.
other.author: benluddy
other.userFacingChange: With the CBORServingAndStorage feature gate enabled, built-in APIs can be served in CBOR format for clients that request it.

enrichment.problem: Built-in Kubernetes APIs could only be served using JSON or protobuf, so clients that preferred the more compact CBOR encoding could not request it.
enrichment.affected: Any workload or tool that talks to the kube-apiserver and wants to use CBOR encoding, as well as the API server itself which now handles CBOR serialization and storage.
enrichment.fix: The `CBORServingAndStorage` feature gate is now enabled by default, allowing the API server to negotiate and serve built‑in API objects in CBOR format when a client includes the appropriate Accept header.
enrichment.impact: Clients that understand CBOR can exchange smaller payloads, reducing bandwidth and latency, especially for large objects. It also enables storage of objects in CBOR format, broadening serialization options for downstream tools.

other.description: Dropped support for `InPlacePodVerticalScaling` feature in Windows.
other.author: AnishShah
other.userFacingChange: Drop support for InPlacePodVerticalScaling feature in Windows.

issueContext.title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] drop support for windows
issueContext.body:
1. In `ValidatePodResize`, if the pod OS is windows, forbid resizing
2. In `handlePodResourcesResize`, if the OS is windows set the resize status to Infeasible, and proceed with the allocated pod.

/kind feature
/sig node
/milestone v1.32

enrichment.problem: The InPlacePodVerticalScaling feature, which allows live pod resource resize, was not supported on Windows nodes, but validation and resize handling code still permitted attempts, leading to errors for Windows workloads.
enrichment.affected: Users running Windows nodes who tried to use InPlacePodVerticalScaling to adjust pod CPU/memory resources at runtime.
enrichment.fix: Support for InPlacePodVerticalScaling on Windows has been removed. Validation now rejects resize requests for Windows pods, and the resize handler marks the resize status as Infeasible and continues without applying any changes.
enrichment.impact: Windows workloads can no longer use InPlacePodVerticalScaling, preventing failed resize attempts and ensuring stable pod behavior on Windows nodes. Users must avoid the feature on Windows or migrate to alternative scaling methods.

other.description: The feature-gate "PodHostIPs" has been removed.  It is GA and its value has been locked since Kubernetes v1.30.
other.author: thockin

enrichment.problem: The GA feature-gate 'PodHostIPs' was still present in the codebase, and configuration files or startup flags that referenced it could cause validation errors now that the gate has been removed.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that still configure the PodHostIPs feature-gate in kube-apiserver, kubelet, or other component flags.
enrichment.fix: The feature-gate has been fully removed from the code. clusters no longer need (and must not) set the PodHostIPs flag; any existing references should be deleted.
enrichment.impact: Upgrading to this release will not affect pod functionality because the feature is already GA, but administrators must clean up any lingering PodHostIPs flag settings to avoid startup errors.

other.description: The alpha Dynamic Resource Allocation gRPC API is still available, but might be removed in future releases. Driver authors should update their DRA drivers to use the v1beta1 gRPC API.
other.author: pohly
other.userFacingChange: DRA: DRA driver authors should update their DRA drivers to use the v1beta1 gRPC API. The older alpha API still works, but might get removed eventually.

enrichment.problem: The alpha Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) gRPC API is still available but is scheduled for removal in future releases, risking breakage for drivers that rely on it.
enrichment.affected: Authors of DRA drivers and any clusters running drivers that still use the alpha DRA gRPC API.
enrichment.fix: Driver authors should update their DRA drivers to use the newer v1beta1 gRPC API, which will remain supported.
enrichment.impact: Ensures continued compatibility of DRA drivers with Kubernetes and prevents future failures when the alpha API is removed.

other.description: NONE
other.author: vivzbansal

enrichment.problem: Previously, updating a pod's CPU or memory requests/limits required deleting and recreating the pod, causing downtime and operational overhead.
enrichment.affected: Pods (and controllers that modify pod spec) that need to change CPU or memory resources while running.
enrichment.fix: Introduces in‑place update of pod resources: with a new feature gate, kubelet can adjust cgroup allocations for a running pod when its resource specifications change, without needing to restart the pod.
enrichment.impact: Allows seamless, zero‑downtime adjustments to pod resources, improving cluster efficiency and enabling dynamic workloads to scale resources on the fly.

other.description: Revised error handling for port forwards to Pods. Added stream resets preventing port-forward from blockage.
other.author: soltysh
other.userFacingChange: Revised error handling for port forwards to Pods. Added stream stream resets preventing port-forward from blockage.

enrichment.problem: Port-forward operations to pods could become blocked due to inadequate error handling and missing stream resets, causing the kubectl port-forward command to hang.
enrichment.affected: Developers and operators who use `kubectl port-forward` to access pods; any workflow relying on stable port-forward streams.
enrichment.fix: Implemented revised error handling for pod port-forwarding and added stream reset logic to ensure stalled streams are cleared, preventing blockage.
enrichment.impact: Users invoking `kubectl port-forward` will experience more reliable connections without hangs, improving debugging and remote access workflows.

other.description: Removed support for removing requests and limits during a pod resize.
other.author: AnishShah

issueContext.title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] Disallow removing requsets & limits during resize
issueContext.body:
/kind feature

For v1.32 we've decided to remove support for removing requests and limits during a resize. We will revisit this in a future release (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/128675)

/cc @dchen1107 

/sig node
/priority important-soon

enrichment.problem: Previously, users could remove CPU/memory requests and limits from a pod during an in‑place vertical resize. This ability caused inconsistencies and validation issues, so the feature is being withdrawn.
enrichment.affected: Pods that are being resized in place (e.g., via the InPlacePodVerticalScaling feature) and any controllers or tools that attempt to remove resource requests/limits during that operation.
enrichment.fix: The API validation and kubelet enforcement now reject pod resize operations that attempt to delete existing resource requests or limits. Only increases or modifications that keep the fields present are allowed.
enrichment.impact: Workloads that relied on clearing requests or limits during an in‑place vertical scaling operation will need to keep those fields or recreate the pod. This change simplifies resource management and prevents undefined behavior, improving cluster stability.

other.description: kubelet: on Windows, consistently resolve filesystem links to volume identifiers instead of inconsistently normalizing to drive letters.
other.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: On Windows nodes, the kubelet inconsistently resolved filesystem links to volume identifiers, sometimes normalizing them to drive letters. This caused unpredictable volume mount paths and could lead to pod failures when accessing volumes.
enrichment.affected: Windows worker nodes running kubelet and any pods that mount volumes on those nodes.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now consistently resolves filesystem links to the underlying volume identifiers on Windows, avoiding any conversion to drive letters.
enrichment.impact: Ensures reliable volume mounting for Windows workloads, reducing pod start‑up errors and improving overall stability of Windows clusters.

feature.description: When `SchedulerQueueingHints` is enabled, clear events cached in the scheduling queue as soon as possible so that the scheduler consumes less memory.
feature.author: sanposhiho
feature.userFacingChange: When SchedulerQueueingHints is enabled, clear events cached in the scheduling queue as soon as possible so that the scheduler consumes less memory.

enrichment.problem: When SchedulerQueueingHints is enabled, events stay cached in the scheduling queue longer than necessary, causing the scheduler to retain excess memory.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that have the SchedulerQueueingHints feature enabled; specifically the kube-scheduler component.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now clears cached events from the queue as soon as possible, reducing memory consumption.
enrichment.impact: Lowers the scheduler's memory footprint, improving cluster stability and allowing larger workloads without causing scheduler memory pressure.

feature.description:
Added a new controller, volumeattributesclass-protection-controller, into the kube-controller-manager.
The new controller manages a protective finalizer on VolumeAttributesClass objects.
feature.author: carlory
feature.userFacingChange:
Added a new controller, volumeattributesclass-protection-controller, into the kube-controller-manager.
The new controller manages a protective finalizer on VolumeAttributesClass objects.

issueContext.body:

Tasks -- 1. Check finalizers for delete VolumeAttributesClass 2. Creating PVC with VolumeAttributesClass * Vac_admission_controller adding finalizer to VAC for protection 3. Updating PVC with VolumeAttributesClass * Vac_admission_controller adding finalizer to VAC for protection 4. Deleting PVC with VolumeAttributesClass * Vac_protection_controller for deletion 5. ### What would you like to be added?

In-place pod resize with cgroupv2 (where systemd cgroup driver is default) should use libcontainer functions to update pod cgroup settings. Please see this issue for details:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/102884#discussion_r1019704157

feature.description: The Job controller now considers sidecar container restart counts when removing pods.
feature.author: AxeZhan
feature.userFacingChange: Considering sidecar container restart counts when removing pods by job controller

issueContext.title: [Sidecar Containers] Pods comparison by maxContainerRestarts should account for sidecar containers
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

Today, there are a few uses of the function `maxContainerRestarts` - mostly to compare pods to decide which one is
better to delete or which logs to get. This is not a huge issue, mostly a quality of life improvement.

The code only look at Container Statuses, but likely need to look at init container statuses as well.
Especially in case of sidecar containers that may behave exactly as regular containers.

There are 2 implementations and 5 comparison interfaces.

Implementatons in:

- pkg/controller/controller_utils.go
- staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/util/podutils/podutils.go

```
func maxContainerRestarts(pod *v1.Pod) int {
	maxRestarts := 0
	for _, c := range pod.Status.ContainerStatuses {
		maxRestarts = max(maxRestarts, int(c.RestartCount))
	}
	return maxRestarts
}
```

We may need to be careful including all init container statuses. If a Pod was failing to start for a while
because of Init container failures and now it is running OK, it is likely not important. However, including
the restartable containers (sidecars) restart count is important.

I think the desireable behavior will be to check regular containers max restart count first. And compare this.
Then compare max restart count for restarteable init containers.

/kind bug

### What did you expect to happen?

Comparison of max container restarts account for init containers as well as regular containers.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Two pods - one with the sidecar container in constant restart loop and one is running sucessfully. Random one will be picked to get logs from.

### Anything else we need to know?

/sig apps
/priority backlog

KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/753

enrichment.problem: The Job controller’s logic for selecting pods to delete only considered restart counts of primary containers, ignoring sidecar (and restartable init) containers. This could lead to suboptimal pod removal decisions for Jobs that use sidecars.
enrichment.affected: Jobs that include sidecar containers (e.g., logging, monitoring, or helper sidecars) could have had incorrect pod eviction behavior.
enrichment.fix: Updated the maxContainerRestarts helper used by the Job controller to include restart counts from all regular containers and restartable init containers (including sidecars). The controller now uses this combined restart count when comparing pods for deletion.
enrichment.impact: Jobs that run sidecar containers will now have more accurate pod‑deletion decisions, preventing premature removal of pods that have experienced sidecar restarts and improving overall job reliability.

issueContext.title: [scheduler] Improve Handling of Node Status
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

This issue is to track follow-ups from #125197, which addressed a performance issue related to the NodeToStatusMap. There are latent issues which we would like to address to prevent future regressions. We can either improve NodeToStatusMap to support some of the below operations more efficiently, or come up with different way to propagate these statuses through the scheduler.

current problems:
- we loop through all nodes to set the [same status](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dae37c21645c0fc04bbb0202ad1eba6ba4438d23/pkg/scheduler/schedule_one.go#L458-L462)
  - w/ current implementation, only need to set Unschedulable status - see [comment](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/125197#discussion_r1621723775)
- we [loop through all nodes](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dae37c21645c0fc04bbb0202ad1eba6ba4438d23/pkg/scheduler/framework/preemption/preemption.go#L419-L430) when determining preemption candidates, so that we can create an [error message](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dae37c21645c0fc04bbb0202ad1eba6ba4438d23/pkg/scheduler/framework/types.go#L392-L397) based on the UnschedulableAndUnresolvable status. this error message can be generated more efficiently. also see [comment](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/125197/files#r1621778045)

other considerations:
- when operating over many nodes, hashing node name string is hotspot when doing hashmap gets/sets. consider creating a lightweight `NodeKey` type, which, for a scheduling cycle, references an existing node. This type should be cheap to hash  (+allow lookup in [flat data structure](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a2911e06a7cd393f7cce088b8399f889527b517f/pkg/scheduler/internal/cache/snapshot.go#L33)), and is safer than string node name, as it is guaranteed to reference a valid node.
- consider updating scheduler to not call postfilter plugins when all nodes are `UnschedulableAndUnresol

enrichment.problem: NodeToStatusMap was changed from a simple map to a struct with accessor methods and a new absentNodesStatus field. Out‑of‑tree PostFilter plugins that accessed the map directly now break.

enrichment.fix: The scheduler now provides methods on the new struct to read node statuses, and introduces absentNodesStatus to represent nodes not present in the map. Plugin developers must update their code to use the new accessor methods. The type will later be renamed to NodeToStatusReader.
enrichment.impact: Only developers of external (out‑of‑tree) PostFilter scheduler plugins are affected; they must modify their plugins to use the new API. No change in cluster runtime behavior for end‑users.

issueContext.title: Pods gated by custom PreEnqueue plugins don't go through backoffQ even in case they ought to
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

With the current implementation, all gated Pods are always regarded as **not** backing off.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ef9965ebc66dafda37800bb04f5e284535bbba10/pkg/scheduler/internal/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L658-L661

That is correct for a vanilla scheduler because all Pods gated by SchedulingGates are not backing off for sure,
but, not correct for a custom scheduler with out-of-tree PreEnqueue plugins,
which could gate Pods that already have gone through scheduling cycles (and got unschedulable).

### What did you expect to happen?

Pods which have gone through scheduling cycles, but now gated should be put into backoffQ. (or activeQ, if it's in the unschedQ for enough time already)

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a Pod that cannot be scheduled.
2. After a Pod got unschedulable, custom PreEnqueue plugin gates the Pod.
3. Trigger a cluster event which could make the Pod schedulable, and with this event, remove a gate.
4. The Pod directly goes to activeQ, not going through backoffQ, while it's once gone through a scheduling cycle.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

master

### Cloud provider

<details>
n/a
</details>


### OS version

<details>

```console
# On Linux:
$ cat /etc/os-release
# paste output here
$ uname -a
# paste output here

# On Windows:
C:\> wmic os get Caption, Version, BuildNumber, OSArchitecture
# paste output here
```

</details>


### Install tools

<details>

</details>


### Container runtime (CRI) and version (if applicable)

<details>

</details>


### Related plugins (CNI, CSI, ...) and versions (if applicable)

<details>

</details>

enrichment.problem: Pods that had become unschedulable and were later gated by custom PreEnqueue plugins were incorrectly treated as not backing off, causing them to be retried immediately without the normal backoff penalty.
enrichment.affected: Custom schedulers that use out‑of‑tree PreEnqueue plugins to gate Pods after they have already been marked unschedulable.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler’s queue logic now correctly classifies gated Pods as eligible for backoff. When a gated Pod has previously been through a scheduling cycle, it is placed into the backoff queue and retried with an exponential backoff penalty.
enrichment.impact: Prevents rapid, repeated scheduling attempts for gated Pods, reducing unnecessary scheduler cycles and API server load, and ensuring more predictable scheduling behavior for custom scheduler extensions.

enrichment.problem: When the kube-scheduler is run with the --allow-metric-labels flag, label values that are not permitted were not properly handled, causing confusion in metric output.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running kube-scheduler with custom --allow-metric-labels that include disallowed values; monitoring tools that consume scheduler metrics.
enrichment.fix: Scheduler metrics now classify any unallowed label values as "unexpected" instead of silently dropping or mislabeling them, making such occurrences visible in the metric data.
enrichment.impact: Improves observability and debugging for users who configure custom metric labels, helping them identify and correct disallowed label values without silently corrupting metric data.

feature.description: kube-proxy uses  field-selector clusterIP!=None on Services to avoid watching for Headless Services, reduce  unnecessary network bandwidth
feature.author: Sakuralbj

issueContext.title: Support skip watch Headless Service in server-side.
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Support watch service with field-selector spec.clusterIP!=None to skip headless service in kube-apiserver. And kubelet/kube-proxy can skip watch headless-service in the future.
![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/42128207/55a3df12-e70d-4b09-b5a4-a5a6ebff890e)

Now, endpoints will be added labels [service.kubernetes.io/headless](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/endpoint/endpoints_controller.go#L518) for headless service  by endpoints-controller,  and kube-proxy will ignore  event for it by label-selector. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go#L913. But headless service haven't be added label and kube-proxy  still watch for it.

For kubelet, it watch service to add service-env for pods , but it ignores headless service when  build service-env-map(https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L549). So kubelet don't need to watch headless service either.

### Why is this needed?

In a large-cluster with more then 5000 nodes,  when we run kubeflow task( tfjob:pod:headlessService=1:10:10) with qps 10, it can save huge network bandwidth and cpu for kube-apiserver.

enrichment.problem: kube-proxy (and the apiserver) watched all Service objects, including headless services that have no ClusterIP, causing unnecessary watch traffic and CPU usage especially in large clusters.
enrichment.affected: Large clusters that create many headless services (such as Kubeflow TFJob workloads). kube-proxy and the apiserver watch paths are directly impacted.
enrichment.fix: kube-proxy now watches Services with the field‑selector `spec.clusterIP!=None`, so headless services are excluded from the watch stream. This leverages server‑side support for the selector and avoids processing those events.
enrichment.impact: Reduces network bandwidth and CPU consumption on the apiserver and kube-proxy, improving scalability for clusters with many nodes and headless services (e.g., Kubeflow workloads).

feature.description: Promoted the `RelaxedEnvironmentVariableValidation` feature gate to beta and is enabled by default.
feature.author: HirazawaUi

enrichment.problem: Strict validation of environment variable names prevented the use of special characters, causing pod creation to fail for workloads that needed such variable names.
enrichment.affected: Any pod or container that defines environment variables with special characters in their names, such as workloads using ConfigMaps or Secrets with non‑alphanumeric keys.
enrichment.fix: The RelaxedEnvironmentVariableValidation feature gate is promoted to beta and enabled by default, relaxing the validation rules to allow special characters in environment variable names.
enrichment.impact: Users can now define environment variables with a broader character set without errors, simplifying configuration management and reducing deployment failures.

feature.description:
Removed attachable volume limits from the capacity of the node for the following volume types when the kubelet was started, affecting the following volume types when the corresponding CSI driver was installed:
- `awsElasticBlockStore` for `ebs.csi.aws.com`
- `azureDisk` for `disk.csi.azure.com`
- `gcePersistentDisk` for `pd.csi.storage.googleapis.com`
- `cinder` for `cinder.csi.openstack.org`
- `csi`
However, it was still enforced using a limit in CSINode objects.
feature.author: carlory
feature.userFacingChange:
Removed attachable volume limits from the capacity of the node for the following volume type when the kubelet is started, affecting the following volume types when the corresponding csi driver is installed:
- `awsElasticBlockStore` for `ebs.csi.aws.com`
- `azureDisk` for `disk.csi.azure.com`
- `gcePersistentDisk` for `pd.csi.storage.googleapis.com`
- `cinder` for `cinder.csi.openstack.org`
- `csi`
But it's still enforced using a limit in CSINode objects.

enrichment.problem: When the kubelet started, it added attachable volume limits for certain CSI volume types (awsElasticBlockStore, azureDisk, gcePersistentDisk, cinder, generic csi) to the node's reported capacity, causing inaccurate node capacity reporting and potential scheduling issues.
enrichment.affected: Nodes running the kubelet with any of the listed CSI drivers installed, and workloads that rely on those storage types for scheduling decisions.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet no longer includes those attachable volume limits in the node's capacity. Enforcement of the limits is now performed via limits defined in CSINode objects.
enrichment.impact: Node capacity metrics are now accurate, preventing pods from being rejected or mis-scheduled due to false capacity exhaustion for the affected volume types. Users of the listed CSI drivers see correct scheduling behavior.

feature.description: Promoted `SizeMemoryBackedVolumes` to stable.
feature.author: kannon92
feature.userFacingChange: Promote SizeMemoryBackedVolumes to stable

enrichment.problem: SizeMemoryBackedVolumes was only available as a beta feature behind a feature gate, requiring users to enable the gate to specify sizes for memory‑backed volumes.
enrichment.affected: Any workloads that define a size for memory‑backed volumes (e.g., EmptyDir, CSI memory volumes) now have the feature enabled by default.
enrichment.fix: Promoted SizeMemoryBackedVolumes to GA (stable), removing the need for a feature gate and making the API stable for all clusters.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now use SizeMemoryBackedVolumes out‑of‑the‑box with guaranteed stability and future compatibility, simplifying storage configuration for memory‑backed volumes such as EmptyDir and CSI memory drivers.

feature.description: client-go/rest: contextual logging of request/response with accurate source code location of the caller
feature.author: pohly

enrichment.problem: client-go REST calls did not provide contextual logging, so request/response details and the source code location of the caller were missing, making debugging difficult.
enrichment.affected: Any component or controller that uses the client-go library for Kubernetes API communication.
enrichment.fix: Added contextual logging to client-go/rest that records request and response information along with the accurate source code location of the caller, improving log granularity.
enrichment.impact: Developers and operators using client-go (e.g., controllers, operators) can now quickly identify which code path generated a request, easing troubleshooting and enhancing observability of API interactions.

feature.description: Graduated the AnonymousAuthConfigurableEndpoints feature gate to beta and enable it by default to allow configurable endpoints for anonymous authentication.
feature.author: vinayakankugoyal
feature.userFacingChange: Graduate the AnonymousAuthConfigurableEndpoints feature gate to beta and enable by default to allow configurable endpoints for anonymous authentication.

enrichment.problem: Anonymous authentication endpoints were fixed and could not be customized, limiting administrators from controlling which API paths accept anonymous requests.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters using the API server with anonymous authentication; administrators who need to restrict or customize anonymous access.
enrichment.fix: Graduated the AnonymousAuthConfigurableEndpoints feature gate to beta and enabled it by default, adding configuration options to specify the endpoints that allow anonymous authentication.
enrichment.impact: Cluster operators can now configure anonymous auth endpoints, improving security flexibility and removing the need to manually enable a beta feature.

feature.description: JWT authenticators now set the `jti` claim (if present and is a string value) as the credential ID for use by audit logging.
feature.author: aramase
feature.userFacingChange: JWT authenticators now set the `jti` claim (if present and is a string value) as credential id for use by audit logging.

issueContext.title: JWT authenticator should set `authentication.kubernetes.io/credential-id` in extra if jti claim is present
issueContext.body:
JWT authenticator should set `authentication.kubernetes.io/credential-id` if the jti claim is present.

/assign aramase enj
/sig auth

enrichment.problem: The JWT authenticator did not include the JWT's `jti` claim as the `authentication.kubernetes.io/credential-id` in the extra fields, so audit logs could not associate requests with a specific JWT credential.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using JWT token authentication and audit logging; security teams that rely on audit logs to trace token usage.
enrichment.fix: JWT authenticators now check for a `jti` claim that is a string and, when present, set it as the credential ID (`authentication.kubernetes.io/credential-id`). This value is then recorded in audit logs.
enrichment.impact: Improves traceability and security monitoring by allowing admins to see which specific JWT token was used for a request in audit records, aiding investigations and compliance.

feature.description: Support inflight_events metric in the scheduler for QueueingHint (alpha feature).
feature.author: sanposhiho

enrichment.problem: The scheduler did not expose an inflight_events metric for the QueueingHint alpha feature, limiting visibility into how many scheduling events were in flight and making it difficult to observe queueing behavior.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the kube-scheduler, especially those that enable the QueueingHint alpha feature and need metrics for monitoring.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now emits the inflight_events metric for the QueueingHint feature, providing real‑time counts of in‑flight scheduling events when the feature is enabled.
enrichment.impact: Operators and developers can monitor and troubleshoot scheduling queueing latency, improve observability of the scheduler, and better tune the QueueingHint feature.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.23.0.
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes previously built with an older Go version; upgrade required to stay current and benefit from language improvements and security fixes.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components and any environments that compile Kubernetes from source are affected by the Go version upgrade.
enrichment.fix: The build system has been updated to compile all Kubernetes binaries with Go 1.23.0.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.) are now built with the newer Go toolchain, enabling future improvements and ensuring compatibility with upcoming Go releases. No functional changes for end‑users, but the upgrade may affect developers building from source or custom binaries.

feature.description: Implemented new cluster events `UpdatePodSchedulingGatesEliminated` and `UpdatePodTolerations` for scheduler plugins.
feature.author: sanposhiho
feature.userFacingChange: Implement new cluster events UpdatePodSchedulingGatesEliminated and UpdatePodTolerations for scheduler plugins.

enrichment.problem: Scheduler plugins had no way to be notified when a pod's scheduling gates were removed or its tolerations changed, limiting their ability to react to these important scheduling-related updates.
enrichment.affected: Scheduler plugins that need to track pod scheduling‑gate removal or toleration changes; pods whose scheduling gates or tolerations are updated.
enrichment.fix: Introduced two new cluster events—UpdatePodSchedulingGatesEliminated and UpdatePodTolerations—emitted by the scheduler. Plugins can now watch these events to handle pod scheduling-gate removal and toleration updates.
enrichment.impact: Plugins can now respond dynamically to changes in pod scheduling constraints, improving custom scheduling logic, observability, and correctness of workloads that depend on these pod attributes.

feature.description: Promoted `RetryGenerateName` to stable; the feature is enabled by default. `--feature-gates=RetryGenerateName=true` is not needed on kube-apiserver binaries and will be removed in a future release.
feature.author: jpbetz
feature.userFacingChange: Promoted `RetryGenerateName` to stable; the feature is enabled by default. `--feature-gates=RetryGenerateName=true` not needed on kube-apiserver binaries and will be removed in a future release.

enrichment.problem: The RetryGenerateName feature was in beta and required clusters to enable it via the --feature-gates flag on the kube-apiserver. This added configuration overhead and could cause inconsistencies if the flag was omitted.
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes cluster that runs a kube-apiserver, especially those that previously relied on the RetryGenerateName feature gate for name generation of resources like Pods, Deployments, Services, etc.
enrichment.fix: Promoted RetryGenerateName to GA and enabled it by default in the kube-apiserver. The feature gate flag is no longer needed and will be removed in a future release.
enrichment.impact: Clusters no longer need to configure the RetryGenerateName feature gate. All API server instances will automatically use the improved name generation logic, simplifying cluster setup and ensuring consistent behavior.

feature.description: Allows PreStop lifecycle handler's sleep action to have a zero value
feature.author: sreeram-venkitesh

enrichment.problem: The PreStop lifecycle handler's sleep action could not be set to 0 seconds, causing pods to always wait at least one second or produce an error when a zero duration was specified.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use a PreStop lifecycle hook with a sleep action, especially when a zero-second delay is desired.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now accepts a zero value for the sleep duration in a PreStop handler, allowing immediate continuation without an artificial delay.
enrichment.impact: Users can define instant termination behavior for containers using PreStop hooks, eliminating unintended pause times and simplifying pod shutdown logic.

feature.description: kubeadm: if an unknown command name is passed to any parent command such as 'kubeadm init phase', return an error. If 'kubeadm init phase' or another command that has subcommands is called without a subcommand name, print the available commands and also return an error.
feature.author: neolit123
feature.userFacingChange: kubeadm: if an unknown command name is passed to any parent command such as 'kubeadm init phase' return an error. If 'kubeadm init phase' or another command that has subcommands is called without subcommand name, print the available commands and also return an error.

enrichment.problem: When an unknown subcommand name is passed to a parent kubeadm command (e.g., 'kubeadm init phase') or when a parent command that expects subcommands is invoked without specifying one, kubeadm did not return a clear error or list the valid subcommands, leading to confusing behavior for users and scripts.
enrichment.affected: Anyone using the kubeadm CLI, especially scripts or operators that call commands like 'kubeadm init phase' with incorrect or missing subcommand arguments.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now validates subcommand names for all parent commands. If an unknown subcommand is supplied, it returns an explicit error. If a parent command is called without any subcommand, it prints the list of available subcommands and also returns an error.
enrichment.impact: Users and automation that invoke kubeadm get immediate, actionable feedback for incorrect usage, preventing silent failures and making troubleshooting easier.

feature.description: Added metrics to measure latency of DRA Node operations and DRA GRPC calls.
feature.author: bart0sh

enrichment.problem: There were no built‑in metrics to observe how long Device Resource Allocation (DRA) node operations and the underlying gRPC calls took, making it hard for users to monitor latency or diagnose performance issues.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the DRA feature (node‑level device allocation) and any tooling that monitors kubelet metrics.
enrichment.fix: Adds new Prometheus metrics that record the latency of DRA node‑side operations and the latency of DRA gRPC RPCs, exposing them via the standard metrics endpoint.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now track DRA performance, set alerts on high latency, and troubleshoot slow device allocation, improving cluster observability and reliability for workloads that rely on DRA.

feature.description: Added a kubelet metric `container_aligned_compute_resources_count`  to report the count of containers getting aligned compute resources.
feature.author: ffromani

enrichment.problem: There was no built‑in metric to show how many containers had their compute resources (e.g., CPUs) aligned by the kubelet, making it difficult for operators to observe and debug CPU manager alignment behavior.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators and developers who rely on kubelet metrics to monitor node resource alignment and CPU manager behavior.
enrichment.fix: Introduces a new kubelet metric `container_aligned_compute_resources_count` that reports the count of containers whose compute resources are aligned.
enrichment.impact: Provides operators with direct observability into resource alignment, enabling better troubleshooting, capacity planning, and validation of CPU manager settings on nodes.

feature.description: Locked the custom profiling feature in `kubectl debug` to true.
feature.author: ardaguclu
feature.userFacingChange: Locking the feature custom profiling in kubectl debug to true.

enrichment.problem: The custom profiling feature in `kubectl debug` could be toggled off, leading to inconsistent debugging experiences and potential confusion for users expecting profiling capabilities.
enrichment.affected: Anyone using `kubectl debug` for pod debugging, especially those who rely on custom profiling for performance analysis.
enrichment.fix: The feature gate for custom profiling is now locked to `true`, making the feature permanently enabled and immutable in `kubectl debug`.
enrichment.impact: Users of `kubectl debug` will always have custom profiling available, eliminating the need to manage the feature gate and ensuring reliable, consistent profiling during debugging sessions.

feature.description: When `SchedulerQueueingHint` is enabled, the scheduler's in-tree plugins now subscribe to specific node events to decide whether to requeue Pods. This allows the scheduler to handle cluster events faster with less memory. Specific node events include updates to taints, tolerations, or allocatable. In-tree plugins now ignore node updates that don't modify any of these fields.
feature.author: sanposhiho
feature.userFacingChange:
When SchedulerQueueingHint is enabled,
the scheduler's in-tree plugins now subscribe to specific node events to decide whether to requeue Pods.
This allows the scheduler to handle cluster events faster with less memory.

Specific node events include updates to taints, tolerations or allocatable.
In-tree plugins now ignore node updates that don't modify any of these fields.

enrichment.problem: When SchedulerQueueingHint was disabled, in‑tree scheduler plugins subscribed to all node update events, even those unrelated to scheduling (e.g., status changes). This caused unnecessary processing, higher memory usage, and slower reaction to relevant cluster events.
enrichment.affected: All clusters that run the default in‑tree scheduler plugins and enable SchedulerQueueingHint. Workloads that depend on taints, tolerations, or node resource changes benefit from quicker scheduling decisions.
enrichment.fix: With SchedulerQueueingHint enabled, the in‑tree plugins now subscribe only to node updates that affect scheduling decisions—taint changes, toleration updates, and allocatable resource changes. Updates that do not modify these fields are ignored, allowing the scheduler to requeue pods only when needed.
enrichment.impact: The scheduler reacts to relevant node changes faster and with lower memory overhead, improving overall cluster performance and scalability, especially in clusters with frequent node status churn.

feature.description: Improved the performance of the job controller when handling job update events.
feature.author: hakuna-matatah
feature.userFacingChange: Improve performance of the job controller when handling job update events.

issueContext.title: The event handlers of job controller are slow
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

The event handlers in job controller are much slower than other controllers. It can cause the ring buffer in the processorListener to grow unbounded when the job churn is high enough.
The processing logic in the job controller events handler appears to be more complicated than other controllers. e.g. in [updateJob](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dbc2b0a5c7acc349ea71a14e49913661eaf708d2/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L464-L504), it invokes function `cleanupPodFinalizers` that lists the pods matching some selectors and the enqueue them to another queue. Similarly in [deleteJob](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dbc2b0a5c7acc349ea71a14e49913661eaf708d2/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L508-L524).

I added some instrumenting code to understand the latency of each event handler.
For job controller P99:
job add event handler: 0.080 ms
job update event handler: 3.075 ms
job delete event handler: 3.076 ms
pod add event handler: 0.136 ms
pod update event handler: 0.709 ms
pod delete event handler: 0.405 ms

For ttl-after-completion controller P99:
job add event handler: 0.0065 ms
job update event handler: 0.024 ms

The above 2 controllers processes same amount of job objects.

### What did you expect to happen?

Complicated logic should not be in the job controller event handler. They should be in the reconciler instead.
So that the event handler can be faster and pendingNotification can be drained faster.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

I use a few thousands of cronjobs with TTL after completion.
I will add more details.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

1.30
<details>

Current HEAD of master
</details>


### Cloud provider

EKS



### OS version

<details>

```console
# On Linux:
$ cat /etc/os-release
# paste output here
$ uname -a
# paste output here

# On Windows:
C:\> wmic

enrichment.problem: The job controller's event handlers, especially the update handler, were significantly slower than other controllers (≈3 ms per event). This caused the internal work queue's ring buffer to grow unbounded under high job churn, leading to increased CPU usage and potential controller lag.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that run many Job objects or experience rapid job creation/deletion (e.g., CI pipelines, batch processing systems). The slowdown primarily affected the controller-manager's job controller.
enrichment.fix: Optimized the job controller's handling of job update events, moving heavy logic out of the event handler and streamlining the processing path, resulting in faster event handling.
enrichment.impact: Reduces CPU pressure and prevents work‑queue buildup in clusters with many rapidly changing Job objects, improving stability and scalability for batch workloads.

feature.description: kubeadm: `kubeadm upgrade node` now supports `addon` and `post-upgrade` phases. Users can use `kubeadm upgrade node phase addon` to execute the addon upgrade, or use `kubeadm upgrade node --skip-phases addon` to skip the addon upgrade. Currently, the `post-upgrade` phase is no-op, and it is mainly used to handle some release-specific post-upgrade tasks.
feature.author: SataQiu
feature.userFacingChange: kubeadm: `kubeadm upgrade node` now supports `addon` and `post-upgrade` phases. User can use `kubeadm upgrade node phase addon` to execute the addon upgrade, or use `kubeadm upgrade node --skip-phases addon` to skip the addon upgrade. Currently, the `post-upgrade` phase is no-op, and it is mainly used to handle some release specific post-upgrade tasks.

enrichment.problem: kubeadm upgrade node did not expose separate phases for handling addon upgrades or post-upgrade tasks, so users could not explicitly run or skip the addon upgrade step during node upgrades.
enrichment.affected: Administrators using kubeadm to upgrade worker nodes; any clusters upgraded with kubeadm where addon upgrades are required.
enrichment.fix: Added support for new `addon` and `post-upgrade` phases in `kubeadm upgrade node`. Users can now run `kubeadm upgrade node phase addon` to perform addon upgrades or use `--skip-phases addon` to skip them. The `post-upgrade` phase is currently a no‑op placeholder for future release‑specific actions.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators gain fine‑grained control over node upgrade workflows, enabling them to manage addon upgrades independently or defer them when needed, and provides a hook for future post‑upgrade tasks.

feature.description: Promoted the feature gates `StrictCostEnforcementForVAP` and `StrictCostEnforcementForWebhooks`.
feature.author: cici37
feature.userFacingChange: Promote the feature gates `StrictCostEnforcementForVAP` and `StrictCostEnforcementForWebhooks` to GA.

enrichment.problem: The StrictCostEnforcementForVAP and StrictCostEnforcementForWebhooks feature gates were in beta/alpha and not enabled by default, limiting users from having consistent, strict cost enforcement for ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and admission webhooks.
enrichment.affected: All clusters that run the API server, especially those that use ValidatingAdmissionPolicy or admission webhooks, will see the new strict cost enforcement behavior.
enrichment.fix: Promote both feature gates to GA, making strict cost enforcement enabled by default and stable across releases.
enrichment.impact: Clusters will now have consistent, enforced cost checks for VAP and webhook admission paths, improving reliability and predictability of admission decisions without requiring manual feature‑gate enablement.

feature.description: Updated the control plane's trust anchor publisher to create and manage a new ClusterTrustBundle object, associated with the `kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-serving` X.509 certificate signer. This ClusterTrustBundle contains a PEM bundle in its payload that you can use to verify kube-apiserver serving certificates.
feature.author: stlaz

enrichment.problem: External components had no built‑in way to obtain the CA bundle that signs kube‑apiserver serving certificates, making verification of the API server’s TLS certs cumbersome and error‑prone.
enrichment.affected: Any workload or external client that needs to validate the kube‑apiserver's serving certificate – e.g., ingress controllers, service meshes, custom users of the API, and automated tooling.
enrichment.fix: The control‑plane trust‑anchor publisher now creates and manages a dedicated ClusterTrustBundle object linked to the `kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-serving` X.509 signer. The Bundle’s payload holds the PEM‑encoded CA bundle that can be used to verify kube‑apiserver serving certificates.
enrichment.impact: Clients, proxies, and tooling can programmatically retrieve the trusted CA bundle from the ClusterTrustBundle, simplifying TLS verification, improving security posture, and supporting automated trust distribution across clusters.

feature.description: LoadBalancerIPMode feature was marked as GA.
feature.author: RyanAoh
feature.userFacingChange: LoadBalancerIPMode feature is now marked as GA.

enrichment.problem: The LoadBalancerIPMode feature was only available in beta/alpha, so clusters could not rely on it for production workloads and had to enable a feature gate.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that create Services of type LoadBalancer and want to control IP mode (shared vs per‑service) could not use the feature in production until it was GA.
enrichment.fix: Promoted LoadBalancerIPMode to GA, removing the feature gate and stabilizing the API, making the feature generally available for production use.
enrichment.impact: Users can now use the LoadBalancerIPMode option on Services without any feature‑gate toggles, benefiting from a stable, supported implementation suitable for production environments.

feature.description: Improved performance of the job controller when handling job delete events.
feature.author: hakuna-matatah
feature.userFacingChange: Improve performance of the job controller when handling job delete events.

enrichment.problem: The job controller in kube-controller-manager processed job delete events inefficiently, leading to increased latency and high CPU usage when many Jobs were deleted.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that run a large number of Job resources, especially those that frequently create and delete Jobs (e.g., batch processing pipelines).
enrichment.fix: Optimized the job controller's event handling path for job deletions, reducing the amount of work performed per delete event and lowering overall processing overhead.
enrichment.impact: Job deletions complete faster and the controller manager consumes less CPU, improving cluster responsiveness for workloads that create and delete many Jobs.

feature.description:
Added new functionality into the Go client code (`client-go`) library. The `List()` method for the metadata client allows enabling API streaming when fetching collections. This improves performance when listing many objects.

To request this behaviour, your client software must enable the `WatchListClient` client-go feature gate. Additionally, streaming is only available if supported by the cluster. The API server that you connect to must also support streaming.

If the API server does not support or allow streaming, then `client-go` falls back to fetching the collection using the **list** API verb.
feature.author: p0lyn0mial
feature.userFacingChange:
Added new functionality into the Go client code (`client-go`) library. The `List()` method for the metadata client allows enabling API streaming when fetching collections; this improves performance when listing many objects.
To request this behaviour, your client software must enable the `WatchListClient` client-go feature gate. Additionally, streaming is only available if supported by the cluster; the API server that you connect to must also support streaming.
If the API server does not support or allow streaming, then `client-go` falls back to fetching the collection using the **list** API verb.

enrichment.problem: The metadata client List() in client-go could not use API streaming, causing slower performance when fetching large collections of objects.
enrichment.affected: Applications using the client-go metadata client to list large numbers of objects; they must enable the WatchListClient feature gate and run against a server that supports streaming.
enrichment.fix: Added a new WatchListClient feature gate that enables API streaming for List() calls. When the feature is enabled and the API server supports streaming, the client streams results; otherwise it falls back to the traditional list verb.
enrichment.impact: Clients that list many resources can retrieve data faster and with reduced API server load, improving scalability for tools that rely on bulk metadata retrieval.

feature.description: Enabled graceful shutdown feature for Windows node
feature.author: zylxjtu

enrichment.problem: Windows nodes did not support graceful shutdown, so when a Windows node was stopped or rebooted pods were terminated abruptly without a termination period, leading to potential data loss or incomplete cleanup.
enrichment.affected: Users running Windows workloads on Kubernetes clusters. Specifically, any pod scheduled on a Windows node that may be affected by node power‑off or reboot events.
enrichment.fix: Implemented and enabled the graceful shutdown feature for Windows nodes, allowing the kubelet to send termination signals to pods and respect their terminationGracePeriodSeconds during node shutdown.
enrichment.impact: Pods on Windows nodes now have a chance to shut down cleanly, run pre‑stop hooks, and persist state, improving reliability and reducing risk of data loss during node shutdown or reboot.

feature.description: Improved  Node's QueueingHint in the `NodeAffinity` plugin by ignoring unrelated changes that keep pods unschedulable.
feature.author: dom4ha
feature.userFacingChange: Improve Node QueueHint in the NodeAffinty plugin by ignoring unrelated changes that keep pods unschedulable.

enrichment.problem: The NodeAffinity scheduler plugin's QueueingHint considered unrelated node changes, causing pods with node affinity to remain unschedulable longer than necessary.
enrichment.affected: Pods with node affinity rules, and any workloads that rely on node selection, could experience delayed scheduling when unrelated node changes occurred.
enrichment.fix: The QueueHint logic was updated to ignore node changes that do not affect the pod's affinity constraints, allowing the scheduler to re-evaluate pods only when relevant node state changes occur.
enrichment.impact: Pods that use node affinity are scheduled more quickly, reducing scheduling latency and improving overall cluster throughput, especially in clusters with frequent unrelated node updates.

feature.author: pacoxu
feature.userFacingChange:

Pod Security admission allows these sysctl in v1.32+ versions of the baseline and restricted policies.

issueContext.title: Add net.ipv4.tcp_rmem and net.ipv4.tcp_wmem into safe sysctl list
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

`net.ipv4.tcp_rmem` and `net.ipv4.tcp_wmem` have been namespaced since https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/356d1833b638bd465672aefeb71def3ab93fc17d (Linux Kernal Version >= 4.15)

It would be helpful to allow config these sysctls for each Pod(Application).




### Why is this needed?


The good performance of some applications depends on these sysctls, for example https://docs.datastax.com/en/cassandra-oss/3.x/cassandra/install/installRecommendSettings.html#TCPsettings.

To handle thousands of concurrent connections used by Cassandra, DataStax recommends these settings to optimize the Linux network stack. We should config these sysctls as the following:
```sh
net.ipv4.tcp_rmem = 4096 87380 16777216
net.ipv4.tcp_wmem = 4096 65536 16777216
```
It would be helpful to be able to configure this for applications without needing to modify the kubelet args.

enrichment.problem: Pods could not set the per‑pod sysctls net.ipv4.tcp_rmem and net.ipv4.tcp_wmem because these sysctls were not on the safe‑sysctl list, even though kernels ≥4.15 made them namespaced and thus configurable per pod.
enrichment.affected: Pods running on nodes with Linux kernel ≥4.15 that need custom TCP buffer settings, especially high‑connection workloads like databases.
enrichment.fix: Add net.ipv4.tcp_rmem and net.ipv4.tcp_wmem to the default safe‑sysctl list for clusters running kernel 4.15 or newer. The sysctls are now allowed by default and are permitted in the baseline and restricted Pod Security Admission policies starting with v1.32.
enrichment.impact: Applications that need to tune TCP buffer sizes (e.g., Cassandra, high‑throughput services) can now configure these settings per pod without modifying kubelet arguments or node‑wide sysctl values, improving performance and simplifying deployment.

issueContext.title: integrate kubelet with the systemd watchdog
issueContext.body:
Implement the [systemd watchdog](https://0pointer.de/blog/projects/watchdog.html) in kubelet. Similar to https://github.com/containerd/containerd/issues/10329, we want to have a lightweight way to health check kubelet instead of requiring to run the health check process `curl`-ing the `/healthz` endpoint.

Implementation will require integrating with watchdog API, hooking those with the same checks that `/healthz` performs, and implement some e2e_node tests demonstrating this behavior. Documentation should be updated once implemented as well.

/sig node
/area kubelet
/kind feature

/good-first-issue
/help

enrichment.fix: Implemented integration of the systemd watchdog API into the kubelet. The kubelet now periodically updates the watchdog timer using the same checks performed by the /healthz endpoint, allowing systemd to automatically restart a hung kubelet.
enrichment.impact: Nodes managed by systemd can now self‑heal from kubelet hangs without external health‑check wrappers, improving cluster stability, reducing downtime, and lowering operational overhead for operators.
