feature.description: Change OOM score adjustment calculation for sidecar containers: the OOM adjustment for these containers will match or fall below the OOM score adjustment of regular containers in the Pod.
feature.author: bouaouda-achraf
feature.userFacingChange: Change OOM score adjustment calculation for sidecar container : the OOM adjustment for these containers will match or fall below the OOM score adjustment of regular containers in the Pod.

issueContext.title: The logic of oom_score_adj doesn't work well for sidecar containers
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

I was debugging a OOM failure recently and noticed some unexpected behavior for how the kubelet is setting `oom_score_adj`.

From the [Node-pressure Eviction documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/node-pressure-eviction/) this is how setting `oom_score_adj` is described for burstable QoS pods:

> min(max(2, 1000 - (1000 * memoryRequestBytes) / machineMemoryCapacityBytes), 999)

The documentation also states the intention of this calculation is:

> This means that containers in low QoS pods that consume a large amount of memory relative to their scheduling requests are killed first.

However the calculation actually does the opposite. For processes that request a small amount of memory the `(1000 * memoryRequestBytes) / machineMemoryCapacityBytes` ratio approaches zero, meaning the calculation ends up being: `min(max(2, 1000 - 0), 999) = 999`

Similarly, when the requested memory increases and the ratio approaches the total size of the machine the calculation becomes: `min(max(2, 1000 - 1000), 999) = 2`

This means that containers that are using the smallest amount of the machine get the highest score adjustment which makes the smallest processes killed first. I observed this in practice while looking at the kernel's OOM logs. These are the set of processes the OOM killer was logging:

```
kernel: Tasks state (memory values in pages):
kernel: [  pid  ]   uid  tgid total_vm      rss pgtables_bytes swapents oom_score_adj name
kernel: [  10325]     0 10325      242        1    28672        0          -998 pause
kernel: [  11029]     0 11029   185553     4518   212992        0          -997 node-cache
kernel: [  10189]     0 10189      242        1    28672        0          -998 pause
kernel: [  11651]     0 11651     2890      117    65536        0          -997 bash
kernel: [  11692]     0 11692   191867    11673   303104        0          -997 aws-k8s-agent
kernel: [  11693]     0 11693

enrichment.problem: Sidecar containers were assigned an OOM score adjustment higher than regular containers in the same pod due to incorrect calculation, causing them to be killed first during memory pressure, contrary to documentation and expectations.
enrichment.affected: Pods that include sidecar containers, especially those using burstable QoS, could lose sidecars before primary containers under memory pressure.
enrichment.fix: Updated the kubelet's OOM score adjustment logic so sidecar containers receive an oom_score_adj that is equal to or lower than that of regular containers in the pod, aligning OOM killing order with intended behavior.
enrichment.impact: Ensures sidecar processes (e.g., logging, monitoring, proxy agents) remain alive longer during memory pressure, improving pod reliability and matching documented OOM eviction semantics for burstable QoS pods.

feature.description: kubeadm: added the feature gate `NodeLocalCRISocket`. enrichment.impact: Allows clusters to run a distinct CRI socket per node (common with node‑local container runtimes), simplifying configuration and avoiding stale or duplicated Node annotations. feature.description: kube-apiserver: Promoted the `AuthorizeWithSelectors` feature to beta, which includes field and label selector information from requests in webhook authorization calls. Promoted the `AuthorizeNodeWithSelectors` feature to beta, which changes node authorizer behavior to limit requests from node API clients, so that each Node can only get / list / watch its own Node API object, and can also only get / list / watch Pod API objects bound to that node. Clients using kubelet credentials to read other nodes or unrelated pods must change their authentication credentials (recommended), adjust their usage, or obtain broader read access independent of the node authorizer.
feature.author: liggitt
feature.userFacingChange: kube-apiserver: Promoted `AuthorizeWithSelectors` feature to beta, which includes field and label selector information from requests in webhook authorization calls. Promoted `AuthorizeNodeWithSelectors` feature to beta, which changes node authorizer behavior to limit requests from node API clients, so that each Node can only get / list / watch its own Node API object, and can also only get / list / watch Pod API objects bound to that node. Clients using kubelet credentials to read other nodes or unrelated pods must change their authentication credentials (recommended), adjust their usage, or obtain broader read access independent of the node authorizer.

enrichment.problem: Node API clients authenticated with kubelet credentials could read any Node or Pod objects. The new AuthorizeNodeWithSelectors behavior now restricts nodes to only their own Node object and Pods scheduled on them, breaking clients that relied on broader read access.

feature.description: Promoted the `ServiceAccountTokenJTI` feature to GA, which adds a `jti` claim to issued service account tokens and embeds the `jti` claim as a `authentication.kubernetes.io/credential-id=["JTI=..."]` value in user extra info. Promoted the `ServiceAccountTokenPodNodeInfo` feature to GA, which adds the node name and uid as claims into service account tokens mounted into running pods, and embeds that information as `authentication.kubernetes.io/node-name` and `authentication.kubernetes.io/node-uid` user extra info when the token is used. Promoted the `ServiceAccountTokenNodeBindingValidation` feature to GA, which validates service account tokens bound directly to nodes.
feature.author: liggitt
feature.userFacingChange:
* Promotes the ServiceAccountTokenJTI feature to GA, which adds a `jti` claim to issued service account tokens and embeds the `jti` claim as a `authentication.kubernetes.io/credential-id=["JTI=..."]` value in user extra info
* Promotes the ServiceAccountTokenPodNodeInfo feature to GA, which adds the node name and uid as claims into service account tokens mounted into running pods, and embeds that information as `authentication.kubernetes.io/node-name` and `authentication.kubernetes.io/node-uid` user extra info when the token is used
* Promotes the ServiceAccountTokenNodeBindingValidation feature to GA, which validates service account tokens bound directly to nodes.

enrichment.problem: Service account tokens did not include a unique identifier (jti) or node information, and tokens bound directly to nodes were not validated, limiting auditability, token revocation, and security enforcement.
enrichment.affected: Any workload or component that uses service account tokens for pod authentication, especially those that bind tokens to specific nodes or need token revocation/auditing.
enrichment.fix: Promoted three features to GA: ServiceAccountTokenJTI adds a jti claim and exposes it via authentication.kubernetes.io/credential-id; ServiceAccountTokenPodNodeInfo adds node name and uid claims to pod-mounted tokens and exposes them via authentication.kubernetes.io/node-name and node-uid; ServiceAccountTokenNodeBindingValidation enforces validation of service account tokens that are bound directly to nodes.
enrichment.impact: Improves security and observability of service account token usage by enabling token traceability, node-aware authentication decisions, and ensuring node-bound tokens are correctly validated. This benefits clusters that rely on service account authentication for pods, especially in multi‑tenant or high‑security environments.

feature.description: Prepared Pod validation to handle version skew for InPlacePodVerticalScaling's beta graduation.
feature.author: sreeram-venkitesh
feature.userFacingChange: Version skew strategy update for InPlacePodVerticalScaling for beta graduation.

issueContext.title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] Implement version skew handling for in-place pod resize
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

This is a tracking bug to implement two changes to better handle version skew as documented in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/1287-in-place-update-pod-resources#version-skew-strategy
1. kubelet: When feature-gate is disabled, if kubelet sees a Proposed resize, it rejects the resize as Infeasible.
2. scheduler: If PodStatus.Resize field is not empty, scheduler uses max(ResourcesAllocated, Requests) even if the feature-gate is disabled.


### Why is this needed?

This is needed to gracefully handle component version skews that can occur during upgrades.

enrichment.problem: During upgrades, version skew between kubelet and scheduler could cause in-place pod vertical scaling (resource resize) to be incorrectly processed when the feature gate is disabled, leading to resize attempts that are infeasible or inconsistent state.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use InPlacePodVerticalScaling (in‑place resource resize) and clusters undergoing upgrades where kubelet and scheduler may run different versions of the feature gate.
enrichment.fix: Implemented version‑skew handling for the InPlacePodVerticalScaling beta graduation: kubelet now rejects a proposed resize as Infeasible when the feature gate is off, and the scheduler uses the max of ResourcesAllocated and Requests when a PodStatus.Resize field is set, regardless of the feature‑gate state.
enrichment.impact: Ensures pods are not incorrectly resized during component version mismatches, preventing pod failures or stuck resize operations and making upgrades that involve the feature gate safer and more reliable.

feature.description: Added support to the kube-apiserver for an alpha feature enabling external signing of service account tokens and fetching of public verifying keys, by enabling the Alpha `ExternalServiceAccountTokenSigner` feature gate and specifying `--service-account-signing-endpoint`. The flag value can either be the location of a Unix domain socket on a filesystem, or be prefixed with an @ symbol and name a Unix domain socket in the abstract socket namespace.
feature.author: HarshalNeelkamal
feature.userFacingChange: kube-apiserver adds support for an alpha feature enabling external signing of service account tokens and fetching of public verifying keys, by enabling the alpha `ExternalServiceAccountTokenSigner` feature gate and specifying `--service-account-signing-endpoint`. The flag value can either be the location of a Unix domain socket on a filesystem, or be prefixed with an @ symbol and name a Unix domain socket in the abstract socket namespace.

enrichment.problem: kube-apiserver could only sign service account tokens internally and had no mechanism to fetch public verifying keys from an external signer, limiting flexibility and integration with external key management solutions.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that require external signing of service account tokens or want to integrate with external key management services. Existing workloads continue to use the internal signer unless the feature gate is enabled.
enrichment.fix: Introduced the alpha ExternalServiceAccountTokenSigner feature gate and a new --service-account-signing-endpoint flag. When enabled, the apiserver can delegate token signing and key retrieval to an external service via a Unix domain socket (file system or abstract namespace).
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now offload service account token signing to external systems (e.g., HSMs, external signing services), improving security posture and allowing custom signing workflows. It also enables retrieval of the public key for token verification, facilitating integration with external identity providers.

feature.description: Promoted `RecoverVolumeExpansionFailure` feature gate to beta.
feature.author: gnufied

issueContext.title: NodeExpandVolume gets called, even if CSI plugin returned NodeExpansionRequired=false in ControllerExpandVolumeResponse
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

In case of online volume expansion of raw block volumes, some of the CSI plugins may not need file system resize or any related handling and thus NodeExpandVolume API call can be skipped for the same. In order to do this, plugin must set NodeExpansionRequired to false, in ControllerExpandVolumeResponse.
However, it is observed that kubelet does call NodeExpandVolume API, after successful resize done by CSI plugin in ControllerExpandVolume API call with NodeExpansionRequired=false in response.
Even though CSI plugin can skip handling in NodeExpandVolume API as per its requirement, is it expected to get this API call from kubelet when NodeExpansionRequired set to false by plugin in ControllerExpandVolumeResponse?

### What did you expect to happen?

During CSI volume online expansion, if CSI plugin returns NodeExpansionRequired=false in ControllerExpandVolumeResponse, to indicate no FS resize handling needed, then kubelet should not call NodeExpandVolume API for such volume(s).

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

The issue is seen with vSphere CSI driver, while expanding vSphere raw-block volume (volumeMode: Block), already in use by one pod(raw-block-pod). However, the issue may not be specific to vSphere CSI driver.

```
# kubectl describe pvc raw-block-pvc
Name:          raw-block-pvc
Namespace:     default
StorageClass:  example-raw-block-sc
Status:        Bound
Volume:        pvc-ad41ea4d-725b-42d7-acb5-9aea7679d17d
Labels:        <none>
Annotations:   [pv.kubernetes.io/bind-completed](http://pv.kubernetes.io/bind-completed): yes
               [pv.kubernetes.io/bound-by-controller](http://pv.kubernetes.io/bound-by-controller): yes
               [volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-provisioner](http://volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-provisioner): [csi.vsphere.vmware.com](http://csi.vsphere.vmware.com/)
               [volume.kubernetes.io/storage-provisioner](http://volume.kubernete

enrichment.problem: During online expansion of raw block CSI volumes, kubelet invoked the NodeExpandVolume CSI RPC even when the driver indicated NodeExpansionRequired=false in the ControllerExpandVolumeResponse, leading to unnecessary calls and potential expansion failures.
enrichment.affected: Users running CSI drivers that support raw block volumes with online expansion (e.g., vSphere CSI driver) and any workloads using such PVCs.
enrichment.fix: The RecoverVolumeExpansionFailure feature gate (now promoted to beta) adds logic to respect the NodeExpansionRequired flag and to recover from volume expansion failures, preventing spurious NodeExpandVolume calls.
enrichment.impact: Reduces needless CSI traffic and eliminates false expansion errors, making volume expansion more reliable for block‑mode volumes and improving overall storage operation stability.

issueContext.title: Allow ConcurrentDaemonSetSyncs to be set for kube-controller-manager
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

A possibility to configure the number of worker threads used in the DaemonSet controller at runtime. A relevant configuration option exists in the code but it is not exposed as a CLI flag right now.

### Why is this needed?

Currently, DaemonSet controller has 2 worker threads and this number is a [hardcoded value](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/daef8c2419a638d3925e146d0f5a6b217ea69b74/pkg/controller/daemon/config/v1alpha1/defaults.go#L23-L36) right now.

In case of large clusters with large number of DaemonSet objects, this might be too low in some scenarios.

We recently got a production issue where adding a substantial chunk of new Nodes failed because Nodes weren't ready on time because Pods belonging to a system DaemonSet responsible for installing the CNI plugin weren't created on time because the DaemonSet controller was occupied with syncing other DaemonSets in the meantime. Similar issue was brought up ~2 years ago in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/111800#issuecomment-1328051923.

Increasing the number of workers would alleviate this issue because the controller would be able to synchronize more DaemonSets in parallel, hence not "starving" the synchronization of the critical system DaemonSets.

enrichment.problem: The DaemonSet controller used a hard‑coded concurrency of only 2 worker threads, which could become a bottleneck in large clusters or when many DaemonSets are present, causing delays in pod creation for critical system DaemonSets.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with many DaemonSets or large numbers of nodes, especially those relying on system DaemonSets (e.g., CNI plugin installers).
enrichment.fix: Introduces the `--concurrent-daemonset-syncs` flag to kube‑controller‑manager, allowing operators to set the number of worker threads the DaemonSet controller uses at runtime.
enrichment.impact: Admins can tune DaemonSet sync parallelism to match cluster size, improving pod scheduling speed, preventing node‑ready delays, and increasing overall cluster scalability and reliability.

issueContext.title: kubelet periodic node status update should not be aligned
issueContext.body:
### What happened? The default `nodeStatusUpdateFrequency` is 10s with 4% jitter. The default `nodeStatusReportFrequency` is 5m. The node status will be updated either there's a change or it has been longer than `nodeStatusReportFrequency` since the previous update. `nodeStatusReportFrequency` https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/55b83c92b3b69cd53d5bf22b8ccff859a005241a/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_node_status.go#L580-L581 The jitter of `nodeStatusUpdateFrequency` won't effectively make the periodic node status update to be spread evenly over the 5-minute window. The node status update requests from thousands of nodes are still sent at almost the same time after a couple of days. It can cause the CPU usage to spike every 5 minutes. The following is the APIServer CPU utilization on 96CPU instances. The cluster has 5k nodes that are added in a short period of time. The cluster is idle without any application workload. The utilization can go up to 64% and go down to 14% just because of these node status update requests. ### What did you expect to happen? I'd expect the node status update requests from kubelet to be spread evenly so that the apiserver won't have a minute that it has to handle the requests from most nodes every 5 minutes. ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? Bring up a cluster and add nodes in a short period of time. ### Anything else we need to know? Ref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/105272/files _No response_ ### Kubernetes version
Cutting edge 1.30 ```console $ kubectl version # paste output here ```
### Cloud provider
EKS
### OS version
```console # On Linux: $ cat /etc/os-release # paste output here $ uname -a #

enrichment.problem: Kubelet's periodic node status updates are aligned across nodes, causing all nodes to send status reports at the same interval (default 5 minutes). This creates spikes in API server CPU usage, especially in large clusters with thousands of nodes.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with many nodes (e.g., thousands) that use the default nodeStatusReportFrequency and experience API server CPU spikes every 5 minutes due to synchronized status updates.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now adds a one‑time random delay of up to 50 % of the nodeStatusReportFrequency when it starts. This staggers the first status report, spreading subsequent periodic updates evenly over the reporting window.
enrichment.impact: API server load becomes smoother, avoiding periodic CPU spikes and improving scalability and stability for large clusters.

apiChange.description: Added `singleProcessOOMKill` flag to the kubelet configuration. Setting that to true enable single process OOM killing in cgroups v2. In this mode, if a single process is OOM killed within a container, the remaining processes will not be OOM killed.
apiChange.author: utam0k

enrichment.problem: When a single process inside a container was OOM‑killed on nodes using cgroups v2, the kubelet treated it as a container‑wide OOM event and terminated all remaining processes in that container, causing unnecessary loss of work.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes nodes that use cgroups v2 (Linux/Windows) and workloads that run multiple processes in a single container.
enrichment.fix: Introduced the `singleProcessOOMKill` boolean flag in the kubelet configuration. When set to true, the kubelet enables per‑process OOM killing on cgroups v2, so only the offending process is killed while the rest of the container continues to run.
enrichment.impact: Improves workload reliability for users running containers on cgroups v2 (Linux and Windows) by preventing a single OOM‑killed process from bringing down the entire container, reducing unnecessary restarts and improving resource utilization.

apiChange.description: Revised the kubelet API Authorization with new subresources that allow finer-grained authorization checks and access control for kubelet endpoints. Provided you enable the `KubeletFineGrainedAuthz` feature gate, you can access kubelet's `/healthz` endpoint by granting the caller `nodes/healthz` permission in RBAC. Similarly, you can access kubelet's `/pods` endpoint to fetch a list of Pods bound to that node by granting the caller `nodes/pods` permission in RBAC. Additionally, you can access kubelet's `/configz` endpoint to fetch its configuration by granting the caller `nodes/configz` permission in RBAC. Alternatively, granting `nodes/proxy` permission allows access to `/healthz`, `/pods`, and `/configz`, but also permits exec, run, and attach operations on containers on the nodes, violating the principle of least privilege.
apiChange.author: vinayakankugoyal
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Revised the Kubelet API Authorization with new subresources, that allow finer-grained authorization checks and access control for kubelet endpoints.
Provided you enable the `KubeletFineGrainedAuthz` feature gate, you can access kubelet's `/healthz` endpoint by granting the caller `nodes/helathz` permission in RBAC.
Similarly you can also access  kubelet's `/pods` endpoint to fetch a list of Pods bound to that node by granting the caller `nodes/pods` permission in RBAC.
Similarly you can also access kubelet's `/configz` endpoint to fetch kubelet's configuration by granting the caller `nodes/configz` permission in RBAC.
You can still access kubelet's `/healthz`, `/pods` and `/configz` by granting the caller `nodes/proxy` permission in RBAC but that also grants the caller permissions to exec, run and attach to containers on the nodes and doing so does not follow the least privilege principle. Granting callers more permissions than they need can give attackers an opportunity to escalate privileges.

enrichment.problem: Kubelet's API only exposed a coarse 'nodes/proxy' permission, forcing users to grant broad access to fetch health, pod list, or config, which violated the principle of least privilege and could enable privilege escalation.
enrichment.affected: Administrators configuring RBAC for node resources; workloads that need health checks, pod listings, or kubelet config access; any cluster that enables the KubeletFineGrainedAuthz feature gate.
enrichment.fix: Introduced fine‑grained kubelet subresources (nodes/healthz, nodes/pods, nodes/configz) behind the KubeletFineGrainedAuthz feature gate, allowing RBAC policies to grant access to each endpoint individually.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now enforce least‑privilege RBAC for kubelet endpoints, reducing attack surface and avoiding unnecessary exec/run/attach permissions while still allowing health checks and pod/config queries.

apiChange.description: To enhance usability and developer experience, CRD validation rules now support the direct use of (CEL) reserved keywords as field names in object validation expressions. The name format CEL library is supported in new expressions.
apiChange.author: aaron-prindle
apiChange.userFacingChange:
To enhance usability and developer experience, CRD validation rules now support direct use of (CEL) reserved keywords as field names in object validation expressions.
Name format CEL library is supported in new expressions.

issueContext.title: Bump DefaultKubeBinaryVersion to 1.32
issueContext.body:
Bump DefaultKubeBinaryVersion to 1.32.

ref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/version/base.go#L69

This is blocking feature promotions in 1.32 and we should look to resolve ASAP

Tracking PR: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/126977

8 tests are breaking, 5 in integration, 3 in unit.

It would also be great to think of alternatives so we do not need to manually update this on every release.

/sig api-machinery
/triage accepted

enrichment.problem: CRD validation expressions could not reference fields whose names matched CEL reserved keywords, forcing developers to rename fields or use indirect workarounds.
enrichment.affected: Authors of CustomResourceDefinitions (CRDs) and clusters that rely on CRD validation expressions that need to reference fields named with CEL reserved words.
enrichment.fix: The CEL library integration for CRD validation now allows reserved keywords to be used directly as field names in object validation expressions, supporting the name‑format CEL library syntax.
enrichment.impact: Makes authoring CRD validation rules simpler and more intuitive, reducing boilerplate and potential errors for developers building custom resources.

apiChange.description: Introduced `v1alpha1` API for mutating admission policies, enabling extensible #     admission control via CEL expressions (KEP  3962: Mutating Admission Policies). #     To use, enable the `MutatingAdmissionPolicy` feature gate and the `admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1alpha1` #     API via `--runtime-config`.
apiChange.author: jpbetz
apiChange.userFacingChange: Introduce v1alpha1 API for mutating admission policies, enabling extensible admission control via CEL expressions (KEP  3962: Mutating Admission Policies). To use, enable the `MutatingAdmissionPolicy` feature gate and the `admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1alpha1` API via `--runtime-config`.

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes lacked a built-in, extensible mutating admission mechanism that could be expressed via CEL, limiting administrators to static or custom webhook solutions for request mutation.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators and developers who need to mutate resources during admission. Works with any workload that passes through the API server admission chain.
enrichment.fix: Introduces a new v1alpha1 admissionregistration.k8s.io API for MutatingAdmissionPolicy objects. When the MutatingAdmissionPolicy feature gate and runtime-config are enabled, users can define mutating admission policies using CEL expressions, allowing declarative, extensible request mutation without custom webhooks.
enrichment.impact: Provides a native, declarative way to perform request mutation, reducing operational complexity and improving performance for clusters that need dynamic admission control. Enables easier policy authoring and potential future enhancements to admission control semantics.

apiChange.description: Allow Pod search domains to be a single dot `.` or contain an underscore `_`
apiChange.author: adrianmoisey
apiChange.userFacingChange: Allow for Pod search domains to be a single dot "." or contain an underscore "_"

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes API validation rejected pod DNS search domains that were a single dot (".") or contained an underscore ("_") even though these are valid in some DNS configurations, preventing pods from using such search domains.
enrichment.affected: Any pod that needs a search domain of '.' or that includes '_' in its search domain list. Clusters using custom DNS configurations that rely on these patterns were previously unable to create such pods.
enrichment.fix: Updated the pod spec validation logic to accept a single dot and underscore characters in DNS search domain entries, aligning the validation with DNS RFCs and real‑world usage.
enrichment.impact: Pods can now successfully use '.' or '_' in their DNS search domain lists, enabling workloads that rely on these naming patterns (e.g., certain internal DNS setups) to resolve names correctly without workarounds.

apiChange.description:
Added a `Stream` field to `PodLogOptions`, which allows clients to request certain log stream (stdout or stderr) of the container.
Please also note that the combination of a specific `Stream` and `TailLines` is not supported.
apiChange.author: knight42
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Add a `Stream` field to `PodLogOptions`, which allows clients to request certain log stream(stdout or stderr) of the container.
Please also note that the combination of a specific `Stream` and `TailLines` is not supported.

enrichment.problem: The PodLog API only returned combined stdout and stderr streams, so users could not request a specific log stream (stdout or stderr) directly, forcing them to filter logs themselves.
enrichment.affected: Any client or tool that reads container logs via the `/log` endpoint (e.g., `kubectl logs`, CI/CD pipelines, monitoring agents) can now request a specific stream.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new `Stream` field in `PodLogOptions` that lets clients specify which stream to retrieve (stdout or stderr). The API now accepts this field, with the caveat that using `Stream` together with `TailLines` is not supported.
enrichment.impact: Enables more precise log retrieval, simplifying debugging and log processing for tools and users that need only one stream. Improves observability workflows while noting a limitation with TailLines.

apiChange.description: The core functionality of Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) got promoted to beta. No action is required when *upgrading*, the previous v1alpha3 API is still supported, so existing deployments and DRA drivers based on v1alpha3 continue to work. *Downgrading* from 1.32 to 1.31 with DRA resources in the cluster (resourceclaims, resourceclaimtemplates, deviceclasses, resourceslices) is *not* supported because the new v1beta1 is used as storage version and not readable by 1.31.
apiChange.author: pohly

enrichment.problem: Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) API version was promoted to v1beta1 and set as the storage version, making the new version unreadable by older clusters. While upgrades are safe, downgrading from 1.32 to 1.31 with any DRA objects (ResourceClaims, ResourceClaimTemplates, DeviceClasses, ResourceSlices) is not supported.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that have created DRA objects (ResourceClaims, ResourceClaimTemplates, DeviceClasses, ResourceSlices) and any workloads relying on those resources. Downgrade operations from 1.32 to 1.31 are affected.
enrichment.fix: The change introduces the v1beta1 API as the storage version for DRA, enabling beta‑grade features. No action is required for upgrades; users must avoid downgrades that contain DRA resources or delete those resources before downgrading.
enrichment.impact: Clusters using DRA resources must not downgrade across the 1.32 boundary, preventing potential loss of DRA objects and ensuring API compatibility. Upgrade paths remain seamless, but downgrade plans need to account for DRA objects.

apiChange.description:
A new feature that allows unsafe deletion of corrupt resources has been added, it is disabled by default, 
and it can be enabled by setting the option `--feature-gates=AllowUnsafeMalformedObjectDeletion=true`. 
It comes with an API change, a new delete option `ignoreStoreReadErrorWithClusterBreakingPotential` has
been introduced, it is not set by default, this maintains backward compatibility. 
In order to perform an unsafe deletion of a corrupt resource, the user must enable the option for the delete
request. A resource is considered corrupt if it can not be successfully retrieved from the storage due to
a) transformation error e.g. decryption failure, or b) the object failed to decode. Normal deletion flow is
attempted first, and if it fails with a corrupt resource error then it triggers unsafe delete.
In addition, when this feature is enabled, the 'details' field of 'Status' from the LIST response 
includes information that identifies the corrupt object(s).
NOTE: unsafe deletion ignores finalizer constraints, and skips precondition checks.
WARNING: this may break the workload associated with the resource being unsafe-deleted, if it relies on
the normal deletion flow, so cluster breaking consequences apply.
apiChange.author: tkashem
apiChange.userFacingChange:
A new feature that allows unsafe deletion of corrupt resources has been added, it is disabled by default, 
and it can be enabled by setting the option `--feature-gates=AllowUnsafeMalformedObjectDeletion=true`. 
It comes with an API change, a new delete option `ignoreStoreReadErrorWithClusterBreakingPotential` has
been introduced, it is not set by default, this maintains backward compatibility. 
In order to perform an unsafe deletion of a corrupt resource, the user must enable the option for the delete
request. A resource is considered corrupt if it can not be successfully retrieved from the storage due to
a) transformation error e.g. decryption failure, or b) the object failed to decode. Normal deletion flow is
attempted first, and if it fails with a corrupt resource error then it triggers unsafe delete.
In addition, when this feature is enabled, the 'details' field of 'Status' from the LIST response 
includes information that identifies the corrupt object(s).
NOTE: unsafe deletion ignores finalizer constraints, and skips precondition checks.
WARNING: this may break the workload associated with the resource being unsafe-deleted, if it relies on
the normal deletion flow, so cluster breaking consequences apply.

enrichment.problem: When a resource stored in etcd is corrupted (e.g., decryption failure or decoding error), the API server cannot read it and normal DELETE requests fail, leaving the object stuck in the cluster.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that contain resources that cannot be read from storage (e.g., due to encryption or decoding errors). Administrators attempting to delete such resources are affected.
enrichment.fix: Introduce a gated feature (AllowUnsafeMalformedObjectDeletion) and a new DELETE option `ignoreStoreReadErrorWithClusterBreakingPotential`. When enabled, the API server will perform an unsafe delete that bypasses finalizers and precondition checks, allowing the corrupt object to be removed. The LIST response’s Status.details now includes identifiers for corrupt objects.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators can recover from stuck corrupt resources without needing to manually tamper with etcd, reducing downtime. The operation is optional and risky, so it is disabled by default and clearly labeled as potentially cluster‑breaking.

apiChange.description: Added a `/flagz` endpoint for kube-apiserver endpoint.
apiChange.author: richabanker
apiChange.userFacingChange: Adds a /flagz endpoint for kube-apiserver endpoint

enrichment.problem: There was no HTTP endpoint to retrieve the command‑line flags with which kube‑apiserver was started, making it hard for operators and tools to discover the server’s configuration at runtime.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes administrators and any tooling that needs to inspect the apiserver’s runtime flags.
enrichment.fix: Introduces a new `/flagz` endpoint on the kube‑apiserver that returns the current flag values in a human‑readable format.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now easily view and verify the apiserver’s flag configuration via the API, improving debugging, observability, and automation tooling without needing access to the process command line.

apiChange.description: The synthetic "Bookmark" event for the watch stream requests will now include a new annotation: `kubernetes.io/initial-events-list-blueprint`. The annotation contains an empty, versioned list that is encoded in the requested format (such as protobuf, JSON, or CBOR), then base64-encoded and stored as a string.
apiChange.author: p0lyn0mial

enrichment.problem: Watch clients that rely on synthetic Bookmark events did not receive any information about the initial events list format, making it difficult for them to correctly initialize state when starting a watch.
enrichment.affected: Clients that start watch streams with the `allowBookmarks=true` option and rely on the initial events list format.
enrichment.fix: The Bookmark event now includes a new annotation `kubernetes.io/initial-events-list-blueprint` that carries an empty, version‑ed list encoded in the request's preferred format (protobuf, JSON, CBOR) and base64‑encoded. This provides clients with the blueprint of the initial events list.
enrichment.impact: Clients can reliably discover the expected format of the initial events list from a Bookmark, improving compatibility and reducing errors when establishing watch streams, especially for features built on KEP‑3157.

apiChange.description: Promoted `CustomResourceFieldSelectors` to stable; the feature was enabled by default. The `--feature-gates=CustomResourceFieldSelectors=true` flag was no longer needed on kube-apiserver binaries and would be removed in a future release.
apiChange.author: jpbetz
apiChange.userFacingChange: Promoted `CustomResourceFieldSelectors` to stable; the feature is enabled by default. `--feature-gates=CustomResourceFieldSelectors=true` not needed on kube-apiserver binaries and will be removed in a future release.

enrichment.problem: The CustomResourceFieldSelectors feature was gated and required the `--feature-gates=CustomResourceFieldSelectors=true` flag on kube-apiserver binaries. Clusters that did not enable the flag could not use field selectors on custom resources.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running versions where CustomResourceFieldSelectors was still gated, especially those that did not set the feature‑gate flag, and any automation that added the flag to kube‑apiserver binaries.
enrichment.fix: The feature has been promoted to GA and is now enabled by default. The feature gate flag is no longer required and will be removed in a future release.
enrichment.impact: Administrators no longer need to modify kube-apiserver startup flags to use custom resource field selectors, simplifying cluster configuration and ensuring the feature works out‑of‑the‑box for all clusters.

apiChange.description: coordination.v1alpha1 API is dropped and replaced with coordination.v1alpha2. Old coordination.v1alpha1 types must be deleted before upgrade
apiChange.author: Jefftree

enrichment.problem: The coordination.v1alpha1 API version was removed, but clusters may still contain coordination.v1alpha1 objects. During an upgrade, the API server rejects these unknown types, causing upgrade failures.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that have created coordination.v1alpha1 resources (such as Lease objects) and attempt to upgrade without first removing them.
enrichment.fix: The release replaces coordination.v1alpha1 with coordination.v1alpha2. Users must delete any existing coordination.v1alpha1 resources (e.g., Lease objects) before performing the upgrade so that only the new version is present.
enrichment.impact: Ensures a smooth upgrade path by preventing API incompatibility errors. Clusters that clean up the old objects upgrade without interruption; those that do not will encounter upgrade failures.

apiChange.description:
Implemented a new, alpha `seLinuxChangePolicy` field within a Pod-level `securityContext`, under SELinuxChangePolicy feature gate. This field allows for opting out from mounting Pod volumes with SELinux label when SELinuxMount feature is enabled (it is alpha and disabled by default now).
Please see [the KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-storage/1710-selinux-relabeling#story-3-cluster-upgrade) how we expect to warn users before any SELinux behavior changes and how they can opt-out before. Note that this field and feature gate is useful only with clusters that run with SELinux enabled. No action is required on clusters without SELinux.
apiChange.author: jsafrane
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Implemented a new, alpha `seLinuxChangePolicy` field within a Pod-level `securityContext`, under SELinuxChangePolicy feature gate. This field allows for opting out from mounting Pod volumes with SELinux label when SELinuxMount feature is enabled (it is alpha and disabled by default now).
Please see [the KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-storage/1710-selinux-relabeling#story-3-cluster-upgrade) how we expect to warn users before any SELinux behavior changes and how they can opt-out before. Note that this field and feature gate is useful only with clusters that run with SELinux enabled. No action is required on clusters without SELinux.

enrichment.problem: When the SELinuxMount feature (alpha) is enabled, Kubernetes will automatically mount pod volumes with a SELinux label. This can break workloads that rely on existing volume labels, and users have no way to prevent the relabeling during upgrades on SELinux-enabled clusters.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running with SELinux enabled that enable the SELinuxMount feature, and any pods that need to keep their original volume SELinux labels.
enrichment.fix: Introduces a new alpha field `seLinuxChangePolicy` in the Pod-level `securityContext` behind the SELinuxChangePolicy feature gate. When set, it allows a pod to opt out of the automatic SELinux label mounting, preserving the original volume labels.
enrichment.impact: Provides a safe upgrade path for clusters that enable SELinuxMount, preventing unexpected pod failures due to unwanted SELinux relabeling. Users on clusters without SELinux are unaffected.

apiChange.description:
Removed all support for _classic_ dynamic resource allocation (DRA). The `DRAControlPlaneController` feature gate, formerly alpha, is no longer available. Kubernetes now only uses the _structured parameters_ model (also alpha) for allocating dynamic resources to Pods.

If and only if classic DRA was enabled in a cluster, remove all workloads (pods, app deployments, etc.) which depend on classic DRA and make sure that all PodSchedulingContext resources are gone before upgrading. PodSchedulingContext resources cannot be removed through the apiserver after an upgrade and workloads would not work properly.
apiChange.author: pohly
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Removed all support for _classic_ dynamic resource allocation (DRA). The `DRAControlPlaneController` feature gate, formerly alpha, is no longer available. Kubernetes now only uses the _structured parameters_ model (also alpha) for allocating dynamic resources to Pods.

ACTION REQUIRED: if and only if classic DRA was enabled in a cluster, remove all workloads (pods, app deployments, etc. ) which depend on classic DRA and make sure that all PodSchedulingContext resources are gone before upgrading. PodSchedulingContext resources cannot be removed through the apiserver after an upgrade and workloads would not work properly.

enrichment.problem: Support for classic dynamic resource allocation (DRA) has been removed. Clusters that enabled the DRAControlPlaneController feature gate and have workloads (pods, deployments, etc.) using classic DRA, as well as existing PodSchedulingContext resources, will experience scheduling failures after upgrade because those resources cannot be deleted via the apiserver post‑upgrade.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with the DRAControlPlaneController feature gate enabled and workloads (pods, deployments, etc.) that rely on classic DRA, plus any existing PodSchedulingContext resources.
enrichment.fix: The feature gate and its controller have been dropped. Users must delete all workloads that depend on classic DRA and ensure all PodSchedulingContext resources are removed before performing the upgrade. After upgrade, only the structured parameters DRA model is available.
enrichment.impact: Any cluster that was using classic DRA must perform cleanup before upgrading, otherwise affected pods will remain unschedulable, leading to application downtime. The change simplifies DRA support to a single model, reducing future maintenance complexity.

apiChange.description: NodeRestriction admission now validates the audience value that kubelet is requesting a service account token for is part of the pod spec volume. This change is introduced with a new kube-apiserver featuregate `ServiceAccountNodeAudienceRestriction` that's enabled by default.
apiChange.author: aramase

enrichment.problem: NodeRestriction admission did not check that the audience requested by kubelet for a projected service account token matched the audience declared in the pod's volume spec, allowing potential misuse of service account tokens.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with the NodeRestriction admission plugin enabled and pods using projected service account token volumes (including kubelet image credential provider scenarios).
enrichment.fix: NodeRestriction now validates that the audience value requested by the kubelet is present in the pod spec's projected service account token volume. The validation is controlled by the ServiceAccountNodeAudienceRestriction feature gate, which is enabled by default.
enrichment.impact: Improves cluster security by ensuring kubelets can only obtain service account tokens for audiences that pods explicitly allow, preventing unauthorized token use. No functional changes for correctly configured workloads.

apiChange.description: Added enforcement of an upper cost bound for DRA evaluations of CEL. The API server and scheduler now enforce an upper bound on the cost and runtime steps required for evaluating a CEL expression.
apiChange.author: pohly

enrichment.problem: CEL expressions used in Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) were evaluated without any cost or runtime limits, allowing potentially expensive or malicious expressions to consume excessive CPU and delay scheduling or API responses.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use DRA with CEL expressions for pod placement or custom resource allocation. Users who define complex or unbounded CEL rules are now protected from performance impact.
enrichment.fix: Implemented an upper bound on the evaluation cost and the number of runtime steps for CEL expressions. Both the kube-apiserver and kube-scheduler now enforce these limits during DRA evaluation.
enrichment.impact: Prevents runaway CEL evaluations that could degrade API server performance or scheduler latency, protecting clusters from accidental or deliberate denial‑of‑service conditions and ensuring more predictable scheduling behavior.

apiChange.description:
Added alpha support for asynchronous Pod preemption.
When the `SchedulerAsyncPreemption` feature gate is enabled, the scheduler now runs API calls to trigger preemptions asynchronously for better performance.
apiChange.author: sanposhiho
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Added alpha support for asynchronous Pod preemption.
When the `SchedulerAsyncPreemption` feature gate is enabled, the scheduler now runs API calls to trigger preemptions asynchronously for better performance.

issueContext.title: KEP-4832(alpha): The core implementation change in the preemption plugin, along with the feature gate
issueContext.body:
- https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4832
- https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-scheduling/4832-async-preemption/README.md

issueContext.title: KEP-4832(alpha): Implement new metrics `goroutines_duration_seconds` and `goroutines_execution_total`
issueContext.body:
We want to add new metrics goroutines_duration_seconds and goroutines_execution_total for the observability for KEP-4832.

https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-scheduling/4832-async-preemption/README.md#are-there-any-missing-metrics-that-would-be-useful-to-have-to-improve-observability-of-this-feature

Note that it should be done by the code freeze, `02:00 UTC Friday 8th November 2024 / 19:00 PDT Thursday 7th November 2024: Week 9` ([ref](https://www.kubernetes.dev/resources/release/)).

enrichment.problem: Pod preemption in the scheduler is performed synchronously, causing the scheduler to block while making API calls. This can increase scheduling latency, especially in clusters with many preemptible pods or high contention.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use preemptible pods (e.g., low‑priority workloads) and experience scheduling delays due to synchronous preemption handling.
enrichment.fix: Introduces the `SchedulerAsyncPreemption` feature gate. When enabled, the scheduler triggers preemption API calls asynchronously, allowing the main scheduling loop to continue without waiting for those calls to complete.
enrichment.impact: Reduces scheduling latency and improves overall scheduler throughput for clusters that rely on preemptible pods. Users can opt‑in to the alpha feature to get better performance in busy environments.

apiChange.description: kube-apiserver: Promoted the `StructuredAuthorizationConfiguration` feature gate to GA. The `--authorization-config` flag now accepts `AuthorizationConfiguration` in version `apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1` (with no changes from `apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1beta1`).
apiChange.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: Before this release the StructuredAuthorizationConfiguration feature gate was not GA, and the --authorization-config flag only supported the beta API version (apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1beta1). Users could not rely on a stable v1 schema for AuthorizationConfiguration.
enrichment.affected: Any cluster using kube-apiserver with the --authorization-config flag for custom authorization plugins; administrators configuring AuthorizationConfiguration files.
enrichment.fix: The feature gate is promoted to GA and the flag now accepts the v1 version of AuthorizationConfiguration (apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1) with identical semantics to v1beta1.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now configure authorization using the stable v1 API without changes to the config file, benefiting from GA stability guarantees and simplifying future upgrades.

apiChange.description: Added driver-owned fields in `ResourceClaim.Status` to report device status data for each allocated device.
apiChange.author: LionelJouin
apiChange.userFacingChange: Add driver-owned fields in ResourceClaim.Status to report device status data for each allocated device.

enrichment.problem: Drivers could not convey per‑device status information back to users because ResourceClaim.Status had no driver‑owned fields, limiting observability of allocated device health.
enrichment.affected: Workloads that use ResourceClaims for device allocation (e.g., DRA/CSI‑based pods) and the drivers managing those devices.
enrichment.fix: Introduced driver‑owned fields in ResourceClaim.Status that allow each allocated device to report its status data, enabling drivers (e.g., CSI) to publish health and other device‑specific metrics.
enrichment.impact: Users and cluster operators can now see device‑level status for allocated resources, improving troubleshooting, automated remediation, and overall reliability of workloads that depend on external devices.

apiChange.description: Apply fsGroup policy for ReadWriteOncePod volumes.
apiChange.author: gnufied

issueContext.title: Add support for applying fsgroup with ReadWriteOncePod volume type

<details>

enrichment.problem: Pods that use the new ReadWriteOncePod access mode do not honor the fsGroup and fsGroupChange settings, causing volumes to be mounted with root:root ownership and preventing container processes from writing to the volume.
enrichment.affected: Any pod or StatefulSet that uses a ReadWriteOncePod volume with a non‑zero fsGroup setting, including workloads using CSI drivers such as the AWS EBS CSI driver.
enrichment.fix: Implemented handling of fsGroup for ReadWriteOncePod volumes so that the volume is chowned according to the pod's securityContext before it is mounted.
enrichment.impact: Pods (especially StatefulSets) that rely on ReadWriteOncePod volumes can now correctly apply filesystem group ownership, eliminating write permission errors and ensuring expected security context behavior.

apiChange.description: Promoted feature gate `StatefulSetAutoDeletePVC` from beta to stable.
apiChange.author: mattcary

enrichment.problem: Prior to this change, the automatic deletion of PersistentVolumeClaims (PVCs) for StatefulSets was only available behind the beta feature gate `StatefulSetAutoDeletePVC`, requiring users to manually enable it and preventing its use in production environments.
enrichment.affected: Users running StatefulSets that need automatic PVC deletion, particularly those managing stateful workloads with dynamic storage. Both new and existing clusters benefit.
enrichment.fix: The feature gate `StatefulSetAutoDeletePVC` has been promoted from beta to stable (GA). It is now part of the stable API surface and enabled by default, allowing StatefulSets to automatically delete associated PVCs when the StatefulSet is deleted without additional configuration.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can safely rely on automatic PVC cleanup for StatefulSets in production, reducing manual storage management and preventing orphaned volumes. Existing workloads that enabled the beta gate continue to work unchanged, while new clusters get the behavior automatically.

apiChange.description: A new /resize subresource was added to request pod resource resizing. Update your k8s client code to utilize the /resize subresource for Pod resizing operations.
apiChange.author: AnishShah

issueContext.title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] Add /resize subresource to request pod resource resizing
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

In-place Pod vertical scaling [feature](/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/102884/) currently relies on PATCH verb applied to Pod objects. This issue tracks a task to design and implement /resize subresource for Pods as opposed to PATCH, add RBAC controls to it, and additionally consider supporting it for Pod superset objects such as Jobs, RS, Deploys etc.

This came up during KEP discussions with Tim Hockin as we revisited first version of the API.
Please see the following discussion threads for context:
https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/1883#discussion_r459156714
https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/1883#discussion_r464627665
https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/1883#discussion_r448752659
https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/1883#discussion_r555668219
https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/1883#issuecomment-814273899




### Why is this needed?

It may be cleaner and more desirable to use /resize subresource to request a desired resize, and such a resource can be optionally supported on objects such as Deployments, Jobs etc.

issueContext.title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] Handle in-place pod resource updates in LimitRanger admission plugin
issueContext.body:
The LimitRanger admission plugin does not currently handle pod updates, but needs to be updated to account for InPlacePodVerticalScaling:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4f04dffe5b2cd652a20b362eaea30164e3e5ea54/plugin/pkg/admission/limitranger/admission.go#L424-L429

/sig node

enrichment.problem: In‑place vertical pod scaling was implemented using a generic PATCH on the Pod object, which lacked dedicated RBAC controls, was less clear, and could not be easily extended to other controller objects like Deployments or Jobs.
enrichment.affected: Users and controllers that perform in‑place pod vertical scaling, as well as developers of client libraries that need to request pod resource changes.

issueContext.title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] kubectl subcommand to resize pod resources
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

In #128266, we are introducing a new /resize subresource to request pod resource resizing. It would be good add support for this in kubectl. 

Few options:

1. A new `resize` subcommand: 

```
kubectl resize pods <pod-name> -c <container> --cpu <cpu> --memory <memory>
```

2. support for `resize` subresource in existing commands like `kubectl patch` and `kubectl edit`:

```
kubectl patch pod pause \
     -p '{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"pause", "resources": {"requests": {"cpu": "200m"}}}]}}' \
    --subresource=resize
```

```
kubectl edit pod pause --subresource=resize
```

### Why is this needed?

This will help us manually test this feature as well as making it user friendly to use the new subresource.

issueContext.title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] Scheduler should use max(Spec.Resources.Requests, Status.Resources.Requests) instead of Status.AllocatedResources
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

Current implementation of in-place pod resize looks at max(Spec.Resources, Status.Resources) which works well when resources are being increased, and works well when resources are being decreased assuming that the decrease request is based on observed lower usage, and the new lowered resources does not exceed current usage.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d86b74b0176c6fa22ba2559ace961fa25c6e98cf/pkg/api/v1/resource/helpers.go#L64-L73

However, a bad actor can game the system by requesting resize to resources lower than current usage, and kubelet grants it not knowing that runtime cannot enforce it, and scheduler may schedule pods to an oversubscribed node. A simple way to avoid this is to use Status.Resources.Requests instead of Status.AllocatedResources.

This also means that containerd and other runtimes need to be at a version that supports the feature so that users get the correct signals (avoid 'forever InProgress')



### What did you expect to happen?

When desired resources are lowered and kubelet admits it and sets status to InProgress, scheduler should schedule new pods against resources that are actually available. Bad actors should not be allowed to game the system.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Resize a running pod by decreasing its memory below current usage.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a 1.32 regression where nodes may fail to report status and renew serving certificates after the kubelet restarts
bugOrRegression.author: aojea

enrichment.problem: A regression introduced in Kubernetes 1.32 caused nodes to stop reporting their status and to fail to renew their serving certificates after the kubelet was restarted, leading to nodes being marked NotReady and loss of secure communication with the control plane.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with nodes that experience kubelet restarts; the issue manifested as nodes not reporting status and failing certificate renewal, potentially affecting workloads scheduled on those nodes.
enrichment.fix: The patch restores the correct behavior in the kubelet so that node status updates are reliably sent and serving certificates are properly renewed after a kubelet restart.
enrichment.impact: Nodes once again correctly appear healthy and can rotate their TLS certificates, preventing unnecessary node outages and maintaining secure kubelet‑apiserver communication.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-apiserver: fixes a 1.32+ regression validating OIDC and anonymous authentication flags are mutually exclusive to authentication configuration. Fixes an issue where the kube-apiserver `/flagz` endpoint would not respond correctly with parsed flags value.
bugOrRegression.author: richabanker

enrichment.problem: In Kubernetes 1.32+, kube-apiserver incorrectly validated OIDC and anonymous authentication flags as mutually exclusive, causing valid authentication configurations to be rejected. Additionally, the /flagz endpoint failed to return correctly parsed flag values, breaking a common debugging endpoint.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters upgrading to v1.32+ that use OIDC or anonymous authentication, and any users of the /flagz endpoint for debugging.
enrichment.fix: Restored the proper validation logic so OIDC and anonymous auth flags are handled correctly according to the authentication configuration, and corrected the /flagz implementation to return the parsed flag values accurately.
enrichment.impact: Clusters upgraded to 1.32+ that rely on OIDC or anonymous authentication can now start with the intended auth settings without errors, and operators can again use /flagz to inspect server flag values for troubleshooting.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-proxy, when using a Service with External or LoadBalancer IPs on UDP services , was consuming a large amount of CPU because it was not filtering by the Service destination port and trying to delete all the UDP entries associated to the service.
bugOrRegression.author: aojea

enrichment.problem: kube-proxy consumed excessive CPU on nodes when handling UDP Services with ExternalIP or LoadBalancer IPs because it attempted to delete all UDP conntrack entries for the service without filtering by the service's destination port.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using kube-proxy (iptables or IPVS mode) with UDP Services of type ExternalIP or LoadBalancer experienced high CPU consumption.
enrichment.fix: kube-proxy was updated to filter by the Service destination port when cleaning up UDP entries, so only the relevant conntrack entries are removed, eliminating the unnecessary work and CPU load.
enrichment.impact: Reduces CPU usage on nodes running kube-proxy for UDP Services with external IPs, preventing CPU spikes and improving overall node stability and performance.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-proxy: fixes a 1.32 regression with a potential memory leak which can occur in clusters with high volume of UDP workflows
bugOrRegression.author: aroradaman

enrichment.problem: Kube-proxy introduced a regression in Kubernetes v1.32 that could cause a memory leak when handling a high volume of UDP traffic, leading to increased memory consumption and potential OOM failures.
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes cluster using kube-proxy that processes a high volume of UDP traffic; nodes running the affected kube-proxy version could see increased memory usage and OOM conditions.
enrichment.fix: The change fixes the regression in kube-proxy by correcting the code path that mishandles UDP packet processing, eliminating the memory growth and preventing the leak.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that run workloads with heavy UDP traffic (e.g., DNS, media streaming, gaming) will no longer experience uncontrolled memory usage in kube-proxy, improving node stability and preventing possible pod or node outages.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix panic when no UpgradeConfiguration was found in the config file
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: kubeadm panics and exits when the configuration file does not contain an UpgradeConfiguration section, causing upgrade commands to crash.
enrichment.affected: Users executing `kubeadm upgrade` with a config file that omits the UpgradeConfiguration section; clusters where the upgrade process is halted by the panic.
enrichment.fix: Added defensive handling for missing UpgradeConfiguration in the config file, preventing the panic and allowing kubeadm to proceed (or report a clear error) when the section is absent.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators can run kubeadm upgrade commands with incomplete config files without the tool crashing, reducing upgrade failures and downtime.

bugOrRegression.description: Resolves a performance regression in default 1.31+ configurations, related to the ConsistentListFromCache feature, where rapid create / update API requests across different namespaces encounter increased latency.
bugOrRegression.author: AwesomePatrol

enrichment.problem: A performance regression was introduced in the default 1.31+ configuration when the ConsistentListFromCache feature is enabled. Rapid create and update API requests that span multiple namespaces experience significantly increased latency.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running the default 1.31+ configuration with ConsistentListFromCache enabled, especially workloads that issue rapid create/update requests across different namespaces.
enrichment.fix: The regression in the ConsistentListFromCache implementation was fixed, restoring the expected low‑latency behavior for high‑frequency create/update operations across namespaces.
enrichment.impact: API clients, controllers, and CI pipelines that perform many create/update calls across namespaces will see restored fast responses, preventing throughput bottlenecks and reducing overall cluster latency.

bugOrRegression.description: The following roles have had `Watch` added to them (prefixed with `system:controller:`):

enrichment.problem: System controller roles prefixed with `system:controller:` did not include the `watch` verb, which could cause controller processes to be denied permission when attempting to watch resources they need to monitor.
enrichment.affected: All built‑in controllers that use the updated `system:controller:` roles (e.g., service, node, endpoint, namespace controllers).
enrichment.fix: The RBAC definitions for the listed `system:controller:` roles have been updated to include the `watch` verb, granting them the necessary read‑only watch access.
enrichment.impact: Controllers that rely on these roles can now successfully watch required resources, preventing permission errors and improving controller reliability and cluster stability.
