bugOrRegression.description: `pod-garbage-collector`

enrichment.problem: The pod garbage collector could fail to delete terminated pods, causing orphaned pod objects and associated resource leakage in the API server.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the default pod garbage collector where many pods complete or are terminated could see orphaned pod entries, affecting administrators and any workloads that rely on accurate pod state.
enrichment.fix: The garbage collector logic in kube-controller-manager was updated to correctly identify and remove completed pods, fixing edge‑case handling that previously prevented deletion.
enrichment.impact: Clusters will no longer accumulate stale pod objects, reducing memory pressure on the API server and ensuring accurate pod listings for users and controllers.

bugOrRegression.description: `storage-version-migrator-controller`
bugOrRegression.author: kariya-mitsuru

enrichment.problem: Clusters required manual steps to migrate stored objects to the new preferred storage version during upgrades, risking version skew and operational overhead.
enrichment.affected: Clusters performing API upgrades where resource storage versions change, particularly workloads with persisted objects.
enrichment.fix: Introduces the storage-version-migrator-controller, which automatically discovers resources needing migration and updates their stored objects to the preferred storage version.
enrichment.impact: Simplifies cluster upgrades and ensures consistency of stored data without manual intervention, improving reliability for users upgrading API groups.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a bug where kube-apiserver could emit an further watch even even if decryption failed for earlier event and it was not emitted.
bugOrRegression.author: wojtek-t

enrichment.problem: kube-apiserver could continue emitting watch events after a previous event failed decryption, causing clients to receive events that should have been suppressed.
enrichment.affected: Any workload or controller that consumes watch streams from the API server, especially when encryption-at-rest is enabled and decryption errors occur.
enrichment.fix: The watch handling logic was updated so that when decryption of an event fails, the watch stream stops emitting further events until the issue is resolved, preventing incorrect event propagation.
enrichment.impact: Clients that rely on watch streams (e.g., controllers, operators) will see correct event ordering and will not process spurious events, improving reliability and security of encrypted data handling.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix kubelet restart unmounts volumes of running pods if the referenced PVC is being deleted by the user
bugOrRegression.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: When the kubelet restarts, it may unintentionally unmount volumes of pods that are still running if the pod's PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) is in the process of being deleted by the user. This causes pods to lose access to their storage and can lead to application errors or data loss.
enrichment.affected: Pods with attached PVCs on nodes where the kubelet restarts while the PVC is being deleted. Users deleting PVCs manually are also affected.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet logic has been updated to detect PVCs that are being deleted and to avoid unmounting the associated volumes for pods that are still running during a restart.
enrichment.impact: Pods that use PVC-backed volumes will no longer experience unexpected volume unmounts during kubelet restarts, improving pod stability and preventing potential data loss or service disruption.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes an issue in the CEL CIDR library where subnets contained within another CIDR were incorrectly rejected as not contained
bugOrRegression.author: JoelSpeed

enrichment.problem: The CEL CIDR library incorrectly rejected subnets that were actually contained within a larger CIDR block, treating them as not contained.
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes component or custom resource that relies on the CEL CIDR library for CIDR validation, primarily API server request validation.
enrichment.fix: Updated the CIDR containment logic in the CEL library to correctly recognize when a subnet is within another CIDR, allowing valid CIDR specifications to pass validation.
enrichment.impact: Users specifying CIDR ranges (e.g., in NetworkPolicy IPBlocks, Service CIDRs, or other CIDR-typed fields) will no longer encounter false validation errors, improving configuration reliability.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.23.8
feature.author: ameukam

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes was previously built with an older Go version; the release needed to upgrade the build toolchain to a supported, up‑to‑date Go release.
enrichment.affected: Anyone building Kubernetes from source and all clusters running official binaries are affected, as the same binary artifacts are produced but now benefit from the newer Go runtime.
enrichment.fix: The build configuration was updated to compile all Kubernetes components with Go 1.23.8, replacing the prior Go version.
enrichment.impact: Using Go 1.23.8 brings security patches, performance improvements, and longer upstream support to the Kubernetes binaries, reducing potential build‑time bugs and ensuring compatibility with future tooling.

bugOrRegression.description: Check for newer resize fields when deciding recovery feature's status in kubelet
bugOrRegression.author: gnufied

enrichment.problem: Kubelet did not consider newer resize fields when evaluating the status of the volume resize recovery feature, which could lead to incorrect feature gating and failed resize operations.
enrichment.affected: Kubelet processes that handle CSI volume resize and recovery, affecting workloads that rely on dynamic volume resizing.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet logic is updated to check the newer resize fields while deciding the recovery feature's status, ensuring the feature is correctly enabled or disabled based on current field values.
enrichment.impact: Users performing CSI volume resize operations will see reliable recovery behavior, avoiding unexpected resize failures and improving storage reliability.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubelet: fix a bug where the unexpected NodeResizeError condition was in PVC status when the csi driver does not support node volume expansion and the pvc has the ReadWriteMany access mode.
bugOrRegression.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: Kubelet incorrectly set the NodeResizeError condition on a PersistentVolumeClaim status when the CSI driver did not support node volume expansion and the PVC used the ReadWriteMany access mode.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using CSI drivers without node volume expansion support and PVCs with access mode ReadWriteMany.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now detects this combination and stops adding the NodeResizeError condition, ensuring PVC status reflects the true expansion capabilities.
enrichment.impact: Users of RWX PVCs with CSI drivers that lack node expansion no longer see misleading error conditions, improving troubleshooting and reducing confusion.

bugOrRegression.description: Resolve a regression introduced in version 1.31 on Windows Proxy, where the creation of HNS endpoints fails if remote HNS endpoints with the same IP address have already been created.
bugOrRegression.author: princepereira

enrichment.problem: On Windows nodes, kube-proxy fails to create HNS endpoints when remote HNS endpoints with the same IP address already exist, causing network connectivity failures for pods.
enrichment.affected: Windows nodes running kube-proxy that need to create HNS endpoints for pod networking.
enrichment.fix: A regression introduced in v1.31 is fixed so that HNS endpoint creation no longer fails in the presence of remote endpoints sharing the same IP address.
enrichment.impact: Restores proper networking for Windows workloads, preventing pod communication failures and ensuring Windows clusters operate reliably after the upgrade.

securityFixes.title: Nodes can bypass dynamic resource allocation authorization checks
securityFixes.description: A vulnerability exists in the NodeRestriction admission controller where nodes can bypass dynamic resource allocation authorization checks. When the DynamicResourceAllocation feature gate is enabled, the controller properly validates resource claim statuses during pod status updates but fails to perform equivalent validation during pod creation. This allows a compromised node to create mirror pods that access unauthorized dynamic resources, potentially leading to privilege escalation.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built using Go 1.23.10
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were being built with an older Go toolchain, which can miss security patches, performance improvements, and may become unsupported.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components built from source; users compiling Kubernetes themselves or relying on pre‑built binaries receive the updated binaries.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go 1.23.10 for compiling all Kubernetes components.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes binaries (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.) now benefit from the latest Go runtime security fixes, performance enhancements, and language features, reducing risk of future build‑time incompatibilities.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built using Go 1.23.9
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version, which could miss compiler improvements, security fixes, and compatibility updates.
enrichment.affected: Anyone compiling Kubernetes from source, as well as downstream projects that embed Kubernetes binaries, will be affected by the Go version change.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go 1.23.9, and all components are now compiled with this newer toolchain.
enrichment.impact: Users building Kubernetes from source will need Go 1.23.9 or later. The newer compiler brings security patches, performance improvements, and better language support to all components, resulting in more robust binaries.

bugOrRegression.description: Do not expand volume on the node, if controller expansion is finished
bugOrRegression.author: gnufied

enrichment.problem: When a CSI volume resize finishes the controller-side expansion, the node side (kubelet) still attempted to expand the volume, leading to redundant operations and potential resize failures.
enrichment.affected: Clusters performing CSI PVC resize where the controller expansion completes but the kubelet still tries to expand the volume on the node.
enrichment.fix: Added a check to skip node‑side volume expansion if the controller expansion has already completed, ensuring the node expansion step is only performed when needed.
enrichment.impact: Prevents unnecessary node expansion attempts, reduces resize errors and improves reliability of PVC resize operations for users relying on CSI storage.

bugOrRegression.description: Do not log error event when waiting for expansion on the kubelet
bugOrRegression.author: gnufied

enrichment.problem: The kubelet emitted an error event when a pod was waiting for a persistent volume to finish expanding, even though the operation was still in progress and not actually failed.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using CSI drivers that support volume expansion; any workload that triggers a PVC expansion and watches events for status.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now suppresses the error event while a volume expansion is pending, only generating an event if the expansion ultimately fails.
enrichment.impact: Reduces noisy error events that could mislead operators and clutter monitoring systems, making real failure signals easier to spot.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes an issue where Windows kube-proxy's ModifyLoadBalancer API updates did not match HNS state in version 15.4. ModifyLoadBalancer policy is supported from Kubernetes 1.31+.
bugOrRegression.author: princepereira

enrichment.problem: On Windows nodes, kube-proxy's ModifyLoadBalancer API updates did not correctly synchronize with the underlying Host Networking Service (HNS) state, leading to mismatched load balancer configurations.
enrichment.affected: Windows workloads that use kube-proxy with LoadBalancer services and the ModifyLoadBalancer policy (supported from Kubernetes 1.31+).
enrichment.fix: Implemented logic in Windows kube-proxy to ensure ModifyLoadBalancer operations update HNS state consistently, aligning the API behavior with the actual network configuration.
enrichment.impact: LoadBalancer services on Windows clusters now reflect the intended traffic distribution, preventing routing errors and ensuring reliable service exposure.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubelet: close a loophole where static pods could reference arbitrary ResourceClaims. The pods created by the kubelet then don't run due to a sanity check, but such references shouldn't be allowed regardless.
bugOrRegression.author: pohly

enrichment.problem: Static pod specifications could include references to arbitrary ResourceClaims. Although the kubelet’s sanity check prevented such pods from running, the API allowed the invalid references, creating a loophole that could be misused or cause confusion.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use static pods which attempted to reference unrelated ResourceClaims (e.g., system daemons defined as static pods).
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now validates static pod specs and rejects any ResourceClaim references that are not owned by the pod, closing the loophole and ensuring only valid claims can be referenced.
enrichment.impact: Prevents unauthorized or unintended ResourceClaim usage in static pods, eliminating a potential security/operational issue and reducing confusing error scenarios for clusters that rely on static pod workloads.

bugOrRegression.description: Removed a warning around Linux user namespaces and kernel version. If the feature gate `UserNamespacesSupport` was enabled, the kubelet previously warned when detecting a Linux kernel version earlier than 6.3.0. User namespace support on Linux typically does still need kernel 6.3 or newer, but it can work in older kernels too.
bugOrRegression.author: rata

enrichment.problem: When the UserNamespacesSupport feature gate was enabled, kubelet emitted a warning for Linux kernels older than 6.3.0, even though user namespaces can still function on older kernels. The warning caused unnecessary alarm and log noise.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with the UserNamespacesSupport feature gate enabled on nodes running Linux kernels older than 6.3.0 were seeing an unwarranted warning.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet no longer logs the warning for kernels earlier than 6.3.0 when UserNamespacesSupport is enabled, eliminating the spurious message.
enrichment.impact: Reduces confusion and log clutter for users running user namespaces on older Linux kernels, improving the overall user experience without changing functionality.

other.description: Improve error message when a pod with user namespaces is created and the runtime doesn't support user namespaces.
other.author: rata

enrichment.problem: Creating a pod that requests user namespaces fails with an unclear error when the container runtime does not support user namespaces, leaving users unable to understand why the pod cannot be started.
enrichment.affected: Users who try to run pods with the user‑namespaces feature on nodes where the container runtime does not support it.
enrichment.fix: The node component (kubelet) now detects when the underlying runtime lacks user‑namespace support and returns a clear, specific error message indicating that user namespaces are not supported by the runtime.
enrichment.impact: Administrators and developers get an actionable error, reducing time spent troubleshooting pod launch failures related to user namespaces and improving overall usability of the feature.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a bug causing unexpected delay of creating pods for newly created jobs
bugOrRegression.author: linxiulei

enrichment.problem: Pods for newly created Job resources experienced an unexpected delay before being created, causing slower job start times.
enrichment.affected: Users who create batch Jobs (batch/v1) and their workloads experienced delayed pod creation, potentially impacting CI/CD pipelines, data processing, and other time‑critical batch jobs.
enrichment.fix: The bug causing the delay was fixed, ensuring that pods for new Jobs are created promptly after the Job is created.
enrichment.impact: Jobs start faster and reliably, improving latency for batch workloads and reducing the risk of time‑sensitive job failures.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix validation for Job with suspend=true, and completions=0 to set the Complete condition.
bugOrRegression.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: Jobs created with `suspend=true` and `completions=0` failed to set the `Complete` condition, leading to incorrect job status.
enrichment.affected: Users who create or manage Job resources with `suspend=true` and `completions=0`.
enrichment.fix: Updated validation logic so that such Jobs are correctly marked with the `Complete` condition during creation.
enrichment.impact: Ensures the job controller reports accurate completion status for jobs that are intentionally suspended with zero completions, preventing misleading job states and simplifying debugging.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fixed issue where etcd member promotion fails with an error saying the member was already promoted
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: kubeadm failed to promote an etcd member, incorrectly reporting that the member was already promoted, preventing successful etcd cluster scaling or recovery.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use kubeadm to add or promote an etcd member (e.g., during scaling, upgrades, or disaster recovery).
enrichment.fix: The kubeadm promotion logic was corrected to recognize already‑promoted members and to complete the promotion without error.
enrichment.impact: Users can now add or promote etcd members with kubeadm without encountering false‑positive errors, ensuring reliable etcd cluster expansion and high‑availability operations.

securityFixes.title: Nodes can delete themselves by adding an OwnerReference
securityFixes.description: A vulnerability exists in the NodeRestriction admission controller where node users can delete their corresponding node object by patching themselves with an OwnerReference to a cluster-scoped resource. If the OwnerReference resource does not exist or is subsequently deleted, the given node object will be deleted via garbage collection. By default, node users are authorized for create and patch requests but not delete requests against their node object. Since the NodeRestriction admission controller does not prevent patching OwnerReferences, a compromised node could leverage this vulnerability to delete and then recreate its node object with modified taints or labels.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built using Go 1.23.11
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes releases were previously built with an older Go toolchain, which lacked recent language and runtime bug fixes, security patches, and performance improvements.
enrichment.affected: All users who build Kubernetes from source or consume upstream binaries are affected, as every component (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kubelet, controller-manager, kubectl, etc.) will be rebuilt with the newer Go version.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go 1.23.11, ensuring the binaries are compiled with the latest supported Go version.
enrichment.impact: Provides more secure and performant binaries for anyone building Kubernetes from source and for downstream distributors, reducing the risk of inherited Go runtime issues.

bugOrRegression.description: Changed the node restrictions to disallow the node to change it's ownerReferences.
bugOrRegression.author: natherz97

enrichment.problem: The node-restriction admission plugin allowed a node (via the kubelet) to modify the ownerReferences field of objects, which could be abused to gain ownership of resources or affect garbage collection.
enrichment.affected: Kubelet nodes interacting with the API server through the node-restriction admission plugin; any workloads that rely on node‑initiated modifications of ownerReferences.
enrichment.fix: The node restrictions are tightened so that a node is no longer permitted to change its own ownerReferences, closing the potential security loophole.
enrichment.impact: Prevents privilege escalation or resource hijacking by nodes, improving cluster security and ensuring ownerReferences are only set by authorized controllers.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built using Go 1.23.12
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes was built with an older Go toolchain, which could miss security patches, performance improvements, and compatibility with newer platforms.
enrichment.affected: Developers and CI pipelines that compile Kubernetes from source, as well as downstream distributors that rebuild the binaries.
enrichment.fix: All Kubernetes binaries are now compiled with Go 1.23.12, updating the build toolchain across the project.
enrichment.impact: Provides security fixes, performance enhancements, and better support for modern platforms for anyone building Kubernetes from source or using distributions that rebuild from source.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fixed bug where v1beta3's ClusterConfiguration.APIServer.TimeoutForControlPlane is not respected in newer versions of kubeadm where v1beta4 is the default.
bugOrRegression.author: HirazawaUi

enrichment.problem: When using a v1beta3 ClusterConfiguration, the APIServer.TimeoutForControlPlane field was ignored in newer kubeadm releases where v1beta4 is the default configuration version.
enrichment.affected: Users upgrading kubeadm to a version with v1beta4 as the default config who still rely on v1beta3 ClusterConfiguration settings, particularly the APIServer timeout.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now correctly honors the TimeoutForControlPlane setting from v1beta3 configurations even when the default config version is v1beta4.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that custom API server timeout values are applied during cluster initialization or upgrade, preventing unexpected delays or failures in control‑plane startup.

other.description: Masked off access to Linux thermal interrupt info in `/proc` and `/sys`.
other.author: saschagrunert

enrichment.problem: Containers and unprivileged processes could read Linux thermal interrupt information exposed via /proc and /sys, potentially leaking hardware state or enabling side‑channel attacks.
enrichment.affected: Node workloads, especially containers or tools that read thermal interrupt info from /proc or /sys, may lose access unless they run with elevated privileges.
enrichment.fix: Access to the thermal interrupt files in /proc and /sys is now masked off for non‑root users on nodes, closing the information leak.
enrichment.impact: Improves node security by preventing accidental or malicious exposure of thermal data. Workloads or monitoring tools that relied on reading these files will need to run as privileged or be updated.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built using Go 1.24.9

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were built with an older Go version; the release upgrades the build toolchain to Go 1.24.9.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.) are rebuilt with the new Go version.
enrichment.fix: All Kubernetes components are recompiled using Go 1.24.9, replacing the previous Go compiler version.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that Kubernetes benefits from Go 1.24.9 runtime improvements, security fixes, and performance enhancements, and maintains compatibility with future Go releases.

feature.description: update setcap and debian-base to bookworm-v1.0.6
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes release images were built using an outdated Debian base and older setcap configuration, which could miss recent security patches and capability settings.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes component images (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) built and distributed via the release process.
enrichment.fix: The debian-base package is updated to bookworm‑v1.0.6 and the setcap definitions are refreshed to align with the new base image. All component images are rebuilt with these updates.
enrichment.impact: Newly built Kubernetes binaries and container images incorporate the latest Debian security updates and correct Linux capability settings, reducing potential security exposure and improving compatibility on modern Debian‑based systems.

bugOrRegression.description: Bump system-validators to v1.9.2: remove version-specific cgroup kernel config checks to avoid false failures on cgroup v2 systems when v1-only configs are missing.
bugOrRegression.author: pacoxu

enrichment.problem: System-validators performed version‑specific cgroup kernel configuration checks, causing false validation failures on nodes using cgroup v2 when only cgroup v1 config files were present.
enrichment.affected: Nodes that use cgroup v2 (e.g., newer Linux kernels) where system‑validator checks were executed during node validation.
enrichment.fix: Updated system-validators to v1.9.2 and removed the version‑specific cgroup kernel config checks, so validation no longer fails on cgroup v2 systems lacking v1‑only configs.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that run with cgroup v2 no longer see spurious validation errors, preventing unnecessary upgrade or provisioning blocks and improving overall cluster stability.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fix Windows kube-proxy (winkernel) issue where stale RemoteEndpoints remained
  when a Deployment was referenced by multiple Services due to premature clearing
  of the terminatedEndpoints map.
bugOrRegression.author: princepereira

enrichment.problem: On Windows nodes using the winkernel kube-proxy, RemoteEndpoints were left stale when a Deployment was targeted by multiple Services because the terminatedEndpoints map was cleared too early.
enrichment.affected: Windows nodes running kube-proxy (winkernel) where a Deployment is referenced by more than one Service.
enrichment.fix: The kube-proxy logic now retains RemoteEndpoints until all Services referencing the Deployment have removed the endpoints, preventing premature deletion of the terminatedEndpoints map.
enrichment.impact: Prevents traffic from being sent to pods that have already been terminated, ensuring correct load‑balancing for Windows workloads that are exposed via multiple Services.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix Windows kube-proxy to prevent intermittent deletion of ClusterIP load balancers in HNS when internalTrafficPolicy=Local, ensuring stable service connectivity.
bugOrRegression.author: princepereira

enrichment.problem: On Windows nodes, kube‑proxy could intermittently delete the Host Network Service (HNS) load balancer for ClusterIP services when the service's internalTrafficPolicy was set to Local, causing temporary loss of service connectivity.
enrichment.affected: Users running Windows nodes with kube-proxy and services that use internalTrafficPolicy=Local. The issue manifested as occasional service connectivity failures.
enrichment.fix: The Windows implementation of kube‑proxy was updated to stop removing the HNS load‑balancer in this scenario, preserving the ClusterIP endpoint and maintaining stable connections.
enrichment.impact: Windows workloads that rely on ClusterIP services with internalTrafficPolicy=Local now have reliable, uninterrupted service access, reducing downtime and simplifying operations for clusters that run Windows nodes.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fix the bug which could result in Job status updates failing with the error:
  status.startTime: Required value: startTime cannot be removed for unsuspended job
  The error could be raised after a Job is resumed, if started and suspended previously.
bugOrRegression.author: dejanzele

enrichment.problem: When a Job that had been started and then suspended was later resumed, the controller attempted to update the Job status and the API server rejected the update with the error: "status.startTime: Required value: startTime cannot be removed for unsuspended job". This caused Job status updates to fail, leaving the Job in a stuck state.
enrichment.affected: Users running batch Jobs that are suspended and later resumed; any workloads that depend on the Job controller's status updates.
enrichment.fix: The validation logic was corrected so that resuming a previously suspended Job no longer attempts to remove the startTime field, allowing status updates to succeed after a Job is resumed.
enrichment.impact: Jobs that use the suspend/resume feature will now complete successfully after being resumed. Users relying on suspended Jobs (e.g., CI pipelines, batch processing) will no longer see status update failures.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix: The requests for a config FromClass in the status of a ResourceClaim were not referenced.
bugOrRegression.author: LionelJouin

enrichment.problem: When a ResourceClaim included a config FromClass, the corresponding request entries were not populated in the ResourceClaim's status, so the claimed resources could not be correctly referenced by workloads.
enrichment.affected: Users creating ResourceClaims with config FromClass (typically CSI drivers and workloads that request generic resources) were unable to see the requested configuration in the claim status, leading to potential provisioning errors.
enrichment.fix: The code that builds the status of a ResourceClaim now correctly copies and references the config FromClass requests, ensuring they appear in the status object.
enrichment.impact: Workloads that depend on config FromClass information in a ResourceClaim will now receive the correct status data, preventing resource allocation failures and improving reliability of CSI-based generic resource claims.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: avoid panicing if the user has malformed the kubeconfig in the cluster-info config map to not include a valid current context. Include proper validation at the appropriate locations and throw errors instead.
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: kubeadm would panic (crash) when the kubeconfig stored in the cluster-info ConfigMap was malformed, such as missing a valid current-context. This caused init/join operations to abort unexpectedly.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators using kubeadm init or kubeadm join when the cluster-info ConfigMap contains an invalid kubeconfig (e.g., missing current-context).
enrichment.fix: Added validation checks when reading the kubeconfig from the cluster-info ConfigMap. Instead of panicking, kubeadm now returns a clear error message if the kubeconfig is invalid.
enrichment.impact: Prevents kubeadm crashes during cluster bootstrapping or joining, giving administrators a proper error to fix the ConfigMap and improving overall reliability of cluster lifecycle commands.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fixed a bug where the node registration information for a given node was not fetched correctly during "kubeadm upgrade node" and the node name can end up being incorrect in cases where the node name is not the same as the host name.
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: During `kubeadm upgrade node`, the code failed to correctly fetch the node registration information, causing the node name to be set incorrectly when the node's name differs from the host's hostname.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using `kubeadm upgrade node` on nodes whose Kubernetes node name is not the same as the underlying host name.
enrichment.fix: The node registration lookup logic was corrected so that the actual Kubernetes node name is retrieved and used, ensuring the node name remains accurate during upgrades.
enrichment.impact: Node upgrades now preserve the correct node name, preventing mismatches that could lead to scheduling confusion, monitoring errors, or failed upgrades on clusters where node names differ from hostnames.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fixes a preflight check that can fail hostname construction in IPV6 setups
bugOrRegression.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: kubeadm's preflight check could fail when constructing the node hostname on IPv6-only setups, causing init/join to abort.
enrichment.affected: Users running kubeadm on IPv6-only nodes or clusters; clusters that rely on IPv6 hostnames for node identification.
enrichment.fix: The preflight logic was corrected to properly handle IPv6 hostname construction, allowing the check to succeed.
enrichment.impact: Users attempting to bootstrap or join clusters on IPv6 networks can now complete kubeadm init/join without premature failures, enabling IPv6 cluster deployments.

bugOrRegression.description: Reduce event spam during volume operation errors in Portworx in-tree driver
bugOrRegression.author: gohilankit

enrichment.problem: The in‑tree Portworx volume driver emitted a large number of Kubernetes events for each volume operation error, leading to event spam that cluttered logs and could overwhelm the event system.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use the in‑tree Portworx storage driver; operators and developers monitoring events for volume errors.
enrichment.fix: The driver was updated to deduplicate and limit the frequency of error events during volume operations, reducing unnecessary event creation while still reporting the original failure.
enrichment.impact: Users of the Portworx in‑tree driver will see far fewer redundant events, making event streams cleaner, improving observability, and preventing potential performance issues caused by excessive event creation.

other.description: Kubeadm: updated the supported etcd version to v3.5.24 for the skewed control plane version v1.33.
other.author: hakman

enrichment.problem: kubeadm did not recognize etcd version v3.5.24 as a supported version when initializing or upgrading a control plane at version v1.33, causing compatibility errors.
enrichment.affected: Users running kubeadm to create or upgrade clusters with a v1.33 control plane who want to use etcd v3.5.24.
enrichment.fix: The kubeadm release updates its supported etcd version list to include v3.5.24 for the skewed control‑plane version v1.33, allowing kubeadm to accept and work with that etcd release.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now be bootstrapped or upgraded with etcd v3.5.24 while running a v1.33 control plane, simplifying upgrade paths and avoiding version‑mismatch failures.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built using Go 1.24.10
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes source was built with an older Go version; upgrading the Go toolchain was needed to incorporate security fixes, performance improvements, and maintain compatibility with newer Go releases.
enrichment.affected: Any user or CI system building Kubernetes from source will now use Go 1.24.10; downstream consumers of the source code are indirectly affected.
enrichment.fix: Updated the build process to compile all Kubernetes components with Go 1.24.10.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that binaries include the latest Go runtime security patches and performance enhancements, improves build reproducibility, and prepares the codebase for future Go version upgrades.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built using Go 1.24.11
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes was built with an older Go version, which could cause build failures, missing security patches, and incompatibility with newer environments.
enrichment.affected: Anyone building Kubernetes from source (e.g., CI pipelines, custom build environments) needed to upgrade their Go toolchain.
enrichment.fix: The source tree is now compiled with Go 1.24.11, updating the toolchain used for all builds and ensuring the produced binaries benefit from the latest Go security and performance improvements.
enrichment.impact: Only developers and CI systems that compile Kubernetes from source are affected; they must use Go 1.24.11 or later. End‑users running pre‑built binaries see no functional change, but benefit indirectly from more secure and stable builds.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a spurious "namespace not found" error possible in default configurations in 1.30+ when using ValidatingAdmissionPolicy or MutatingAdmissionPolicy to intercept namespaced objects in newly-created namespaces
bugOrRegression.author: lalitc375

enrichment.problem: When using ValidatingAdmissionPolicy or MutatingAdmissionPolicy to intercept namespaced objects in newly created namespaces, clusters with the default configuration in Kubernetes 1.30+ could return a spurious "namespace not found" error, causing admission to fail even though the namespace exists.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using ValidatingAdmissionPolicy or MutatingAdmissionPolicy with default settings in Kubernetes 1.30 or later, especially when creating objects in namespaces that have just been created.
enrichment.fix: The API server admission handling logic was updated to correctly recognize newly created namespaces during policy evaluation, eliminating the false "namespace not found" error.
enrichment.impact: Admission policies now work reliably for objects in freshly created namespaces, preventing unexpected rejections of legitimate workloads and reducing operational friction for cluster administrators using VAP/MAP.

bugOrRegression.description: Make / build: fix docker IP address detection
bugOrRegression.author: BenTheElder

enrichment.problem: The build scripts failed to correctly detect the Docker daemon's IP address, causing build and test steps that rely on Docker networking to use an incorrect address.
enrichment.affected: Developers and CI systems building Kubernetes using Docker; test environments that depend on Docker networking.
enrichment.fix: Updated the Makefile/build logic to reliably determine the Docker host IP across environments, ensuring proper communication with containers during build and test processes.
enrichment.impact: Developers and CI pipelines that build Kubernetes with Docker will no longer encounter networking-related build failures, improving reliability of builds and tests.

bugOrRegression.description: The slow initialization of container runtime will not cause System WatchDog to kill kubelet. Device Manager is not considered healthy before it attempted to start listening on the port.
bugOrRegression.author: SergeyKanzhelev

enrichment.problem: When the container runtime took a long time to initialize, the system watchdog timer mistakenly terminated the kubelet process. Additionally, the Device Manager was reported as unhealthy before it had started listening on its port.
enrichment.affected: Nodes with slow container runtime initialization; any workloads running on those nodes could be disrupted by kubelet restarts. The Device Manager health status also affected node health monitoring.
enrichment.fix: The watchdog logic was updated so that a slow container runtime startup no longer triggers kubelet termination. The Device Manager health check was also changed to mark the component healthy only after it begins listening on its port.
enrichment.impact: Nodes no longer experience unexpected kubelet restarts due to slow CRI startup, improving node stability and reducing pod disruptions. Device Manager health reporting is more accurate, preventing false alarms.
